articleTitle: DDRSNet-Rail Surface Defects Classification Based on Depthwise-Dilated Convolution
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: In the domain of railway safety, effective rail surface defects detection remains a pivotal challenge. This paper presents a novel convolutional architecture named Depthwise-Dilated Convolution (DDC) aimed at efficiently classifying rail surface defects. Leveraging the benefits of both depthwise and dilated convolutions, our DDC model showcases significant advantages in terms of computational efficiency and accuracy. Experiments on a comprehensive dataset of 4,698 rail surface defects images, sourced from passenger railways in Northwest China, resulted in an impressive test accuracy of 94.43%. Comparative benchmarks against state-of-the-art models, including CNN, CNN-SPP, Fractal Convolution, Transpose Convolution, and MobileNetV2, further substantiate the superiority of our approach. Through rigorous feature map evaluations, we illustrate the DDC's enhanced capability in discerning intricate rail defects features. Our findings position the Depthwise-Dilated Convolution as a frontrunner for real-world applications, especially in computational-constrained environments.

articleTitle: A Fabric Defect Detection Algorithm Based on YOLOv8
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: In response to the practical problems faced by manual defect detection in the textile industry, this paper studies an automatic fabric defect detection algorithm based on machine vision. Starting from the research background of deep learning based fabric defect detection algorithms, this article introduces the latest YOLOv8 algorithm model released by Ultratics. Based on the complex and diverse textures of textiles, a coordinate attention mechanism is added to the YOLOv8n model to enhance the network's ability to extract features. The experimental results show that the fabric defect detection algorithm designed in this article has high detection accuracy, mAP up to 79.20%, fast speed, and FPS up to 95.4, which can meet the requirements of online real-time detection with low computational resource requirements and can be deployed on edge intelligent computing devices. The algorithm designed in this article has good comprehensive performance and can promote the deployment of textile defect automatic detection technology in the industry.

articleTitle: Credit Card Fraud Detection Using Adversarial Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: In recent years, with the proliferation of the internet and e-commerce, the user base for credit cards has witnessed a continuous surge. However, the presence of credit card fraud has resulted in immeasurable losses for users, merchants, and financial institutions. Contemporary practices in fraud detection primarily rely on classification methods such as CNN, LSTM, and DNN. Nonetheless, these approaches predominantly consider the utilization of original features and exhibit suboptimal performance when confronted with imbalanced datasets. Moreover, they necessitate substantial volumes of annotated data for effective training. This paper introduces an unsupervised anomaly detection network that leverages dual adversarial learning for credit card fraud detection. In contrast to conventional anomaly detection methodologies, our approach emphasizes the simultaneous consideration of both original and intermediate features. Experimental results conducted on the European cardholder dataset demonstrate the superior efficacy of our approach, with an achieved accuracy of 0.9224, F1 score of 0.9208, and MCC of 0.8456, surpassing existing fraud detection techniques.

articleTitle: Distress Keywords Classification Based on Audio MFCC Features using Convolutional Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: A growing interest in audio classification is being investigated to improve the surveillance system. With the capacity to identify keywords in speech, it can be designed to recognise particular distress phrases and initiate the necessary procedures to stop undesired situations from happening. This paper illustrates a simple audio classification model using a convolutional neural network (CNN). We first sampled 1040 audio from 13 males and 13 females. Mel-frequency Cepstral Coefficients (MFCC) were used to extract features and generate spectrogram images as input to the CNN network. We chose four keywords: 'Help', 'Yelp' and 'Stop', 'Stock' and collected 1040 samples to train the model. Our final CNN model achieves 86% accuracy on the testing dataset. The experimental results show that our model is good at classifying ‘Help’ and ‘Yelp’, with accuracy greater than 90%, but has weaker performance when differentiating ‘Stop’ from ‘Stock’.

articleTitle: FSPN: Feature Selection Pyramid Network for Tiny Person Detection
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Object detection is an important research direction in the field of computer vision, which aims to classify and locate objects in the input image. Among them, small target detection is a difficult point in target detection. Due to the small size of the target and the less available features, it is difficult to learn the characteristics of small targets well. Therefore, it is necessary to fully learn multi-scale information and context information to improve the performance of small target detection. Although the classical Feature Pyramid Network (FPN) fuses the deep semantic information with the shallow representation information through a lateral connection, the simple addition fusion method does not take into account the problem caused by the difference in scale information between adjacent feature layers. Therefore, to better integrate the scale information of features and fully exploit the spatial context information, this paper proposes a Feature Selection Pyramid Network (FSPN), which optimizes small target detection through feature reconciliation and spatial context feature selection. Experiments demonstrate that the FSPN achieves a 2.07% higher detection accuracy than FPN on the TinyPerson dataset.

articleTitle: SpecRef: A Fast Training-free Baseline of Specific Reference-Condition Real Image Editing
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Text-conditional image editing based on large diffusion generative model has attracted the attention of both the industry and the research community. Most existing methods are non-reference editing, with the user only able to provide a source image and text prompt. However, it restricts user’s control over the characteristics of editing outcome. To increase user freedom, we propose a new task called Specific Reference Condition Real Image Editing, which allows user to provide a reference image to further control the outcome, such as replacing an object with a particular one. To accomplish this, we propose a fast baseline method named SpecRef. Specifically, we design a Specific Reference Attention Controller to incorporate features from the reference image, and adopt a mask mechanism to prevent interference between editing and non-editing regions. We evaluate SpecRef on typical editing tasks and show that it can achieve satisfactory performance. The source code is available on https://github.com/jingjiqinggong/specp2p.

articleTitle: Stereo Matching Based on Collective Adaptive Symbiotic Genetic Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Stereo matching algorithms are used to recovery the three-dimensional map through the left and right pictures from the binocular camera. The accurate matching of corresponding points between stereo image pairs is a fundamental step in stereo vision, but it remains a challenging task due to factors such as occlusions, noise, and image ambiguities. This paper proposes an accurate stereo matching algorithm based on collective adaptive symbiotic genetic algorithms. The fundamental idea behind using GA for stereo matching is to formulate the problem as an optimization task. To address this, we decompose complete images into numerous smaller image patches, each represented as distinct species or populations with phenotypes corresponding to different polynomial functionals. For each patch, the cost function contains both self and symbiotic terms with adaptive weights. By minimizing the cost function, GA propagates local interactions to a global scale and finds the global optimal polynomial functionals for each patch. Finally, by fusing all the small patches, we obtain the accurate disparity map.

articleTitle: GLCM-1DCNN-based hyperspectral inversion of organic matter in improved saline soils
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: The organic matter content of saline soils is an important biochemical indicator for evaluating the effectiveness of saline land improvement. Therefore, monitoring soil organic matter content rapidly and accurately is the key to realizing accurate monitoring of the degree of saline soil improvement. Hyperspectral image technology allows rapid inversion of soil organic matter content.Using measured hyperspectral data and soil organic matter content of saline-amended soils as raw data and extraction of spatial information by GLCM to form texture features fused with hyperspectral reflectance mapping. Construction of a convolutional network model and inversion of soil organic matter content in saline-amended soils and comparison with hyperspectral reflectance data processing. The results show that compared to other data processing methods, the best prediction model is inverted using the inversion of the texture features extracted with GLCM fused with the hyperspectral reflectance maps, the method of image and spectrum fusion, with is 0.9869, which is a 9.85% enhancement compared to the hyperspectral reflectance inversion method, and is 9.7192, which is a decrease of 65.9210 compared to the hyperspectral reflectance inversion method.

articleTitle: Research on efficient registration algorithm of SAC-IA columnar targets based on prior knowledge
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: With the rapid development of 3D machine vision, 3D reconstruction and 6D pose estimation technology have attracted people's attention. In these fields, point cloud registration is considered the core technology. At present, point cloud registration methods based on local features mostly use the SAC-IA method to calculate the optimal transformation of feature points. However, this algorithm has problems such as high randomness in feature point selection and low computational efficiency. This article focuses on columnar object targets, The direction information of the target in the optical image obtained by the multi-modal sensor is used to estimate the pitch and yaw direction of the target, and thereby constrain the feature point transformation space of SAC-IA, thereby improving efficiency and accuracy. Experiments have shown that the method in this paper is 60-70% faster and 5-20% more accurate than the original algorithm.

articleTitle: Dual-Projector Structured Light Illumination for 3D Measurement of Highly Reflective Surface
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: In structured light 3D measurement, highly reflective surfaces cause image saturation in captured camera images, which negatively impacts point cloud reconstruction. In this paper, we propose a dual-projector method as a solution to this problem. Firstly, by capturing images from two different projectors, the camera obtains two groups of information that can compensate each other. Second, the phase order is employed to determine the invalid phase, and subsequently categorize pixels based on the results. Finally, according to different pixel categories, the appropriate model is selected for point cloud reconstruction. The experiment results demonstrate that the proposed method effectively reduces the flying points in the point cloud derived from highly reflective surface and enhances the quality of the reconstructed point cloud.

articleTitle: A Generic LiDAR-Camera Extrinsic Calibration Method base on Lightweight SAM
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: In the domains of autonomous driving and robotic vision, camera and LIDAR, as core sensors, played an imperative roles where the precise fusion of their data had a significant impact on environmental perception. Accordingly, the accurate calibration of external parameters to achieve data fusion emerged as a crucial step to enhance system performance. This paper proposed a zero-shot, target-less and rapid method for calibrating the external parameter of the LiDAR-Camera, based on the distillation of the large model, Segment Anything Model (SAM). Initially, the SAM model was distilled, resulting in a lightweight image segmentation model that could rapidly segment objects in any scene and obtain a mask for each object. Subsequently, a process for handling LiDAR point cloud data was designed, which could obtain the attributes of each point cloud and adaptively acquire the weights of each attribute based on the scene. After processing the image and point cloud data, the external parameter from the LiDAR to the camera was optimized by maximizing the consistency of the point cloud projection to the segmented image mask. The proposed method was evaluated on numerous public datasets and self-built datasets, and compared with other advanced methods. The results indicated that our method exhibited higher accuracy and speed in different scenes.

articleTitle: Application of Improved Adaptive Genetic Algorithm in Flexible Workshop Scheduling
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: In the problem of flexible job shop scheduling, conventional genetic algorithms exhibit limited exploration capabilities and are prone to getting stuck in local optima. Consequently, this study aims to enhance the traditional genetic algorithm by adapting it to better address the scheduling problem. To do so, a corresponding mathematical model is established, taking into account the unique characteristics of flexible job shop scheduling problems. Within the genetic operations, adaptive improved crossover and mutation operators are employed, enabling non-linear adjustments based on the fitness values of each individual in the population during the iteration process. Moreover, an elitist retention strategy is implemented to minimize completion time and secure the optimal solution. Through this improved approach, the algorithm's global search ability is enhanced, convergence speed is accelerated, population diversity is increased, and optimal solutions for flexible job shop scheduling problems are obtained more quickly. Finally, the algorithm's efficiency and feasibility are demonstrated by successfully obtaining the optimal solution for the LA01 example in the workshop scheduling problem through testing..

articleTitle: Synergistic Image Encryption Using a Hybrid of Logistic, Tent, and Intermittent Chaotic Mappings
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: The encryption of images is an essential component of ensuring data security in the digital age. Delving into chaotic mappings, our study unveils their robust potential for image encryption. In this paper, we propose a novel scheme for encryption-decryption by merging three chaotic mappings - Logistic, Tent, and Intermittent - into a single scheme. Our rigorous empirical evaluations, spanning histogram uniformity, entropy metrics, and key sensitivity, establish the unparalleled efficacy of our amalgamated approach.

articleTitle: A method for suppressing SAR radio frequency interference based on deep learning in time-frequency domain
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Synthetic-aperture radar is widely deployed due to its high resolution, such as deployed in battlefield monitoring, geographic mapping, disaster assessment and other fields. Radio frequency interference, as an active interference method, mainly emits electromagnetic waves to make the radar receiver inevitably receive interference signals while receiving echoes, forming a masking effect on the images, thereby reducing the quality of SAR images. Many filtering algorithms have been proposed to address the aforementioned issue, however, these algorithms generally lack generalization and the real-time performance is insufficient. Therefore, in order to solve the above problems, this paper proposes a deep learning filtering algorithm and constructs a simulation dataset in the time-frequency domain. The final experimental results show that the PSNR of the time-frequency map is improved to 35.4dB by our method, and the interference on the SAR image is effectively filtered out. What's more, this method has good generalization and can work well against various RFI styles.

articleTitle: Disparity Estimation with Deep Feature Parallel Transformation
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: We propose a feature parallel transformation module to strength the matching ability in stereo. We obtain additional information from input images, enhance features from the feature extraction module and design a parallel cascading module to fuse the features, which have rich global information. In addition, our feature transformation modules can be applied to any existing stereo networks in a plug and play manner. Our simple yet effect module can perform outstandingly on stereo benchmarks.

articleTitle: Bird's nest recognition method combining visual salience and deep learning
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: The identification of bird's nest targets on transmission lines based on drone inspection images is of great significance in reducing power inspection costs and improving inspection efficiency. This article conducts research on bird nest automatic recognition based on deep learning and visual saliency methods. Firstly, a saliency map is constructed to guide the segmentation of salient regions, and then feature enhancement is performed on the segmented salient regions. Next, the original image and enhancement results are fused and input into a deep learning model for training. The model constructs a feature pyramid to meet the needs of multi-scale bird nest target recognition. Finally, the classification and regression sub models are used to output the bird nest recognition results. Through conducting specific experiments, the results show that the proposed fusion saliency and deep learning bird nest recognition method performs well, with the average precision, Recall, and IoU accuracy indicators above 0.95.

articleTitle: Research on multi-task learning method based on causal features
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Multi-task deep learning has gradually evolved from general layer parameter sharing to connecting and switching between specific layers. However, due to the limited knowledge of task relationships and hierarchies, it is difficult to reasonably set up shared modules in the network, which leads to insufficient model accuracy and generalization ability. To address this problem, a multi-task learning method based on the combination of causal learning and adaptive strategy is given here: at the feature level adopts causal discovery, causal feature reflux to extract stable task features required for model training to improve the accuracy and generalization ability of the model; and then adaptive learning strategy is used to dynamically learn the shared network modules between tasks, which avoids inaccuracy of the manual settings. The experimental results and analyses validate the effectiveness of the approach through rich experiments on the NYU_V2.

articleTitle: Adaptive Network-Based Pedestrian Detection in Haze Environment
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: The task of image dehazing, which involves the extraction of atmospheric haze from an image, presents a significant challenge due to the necessity of haze removal without detriment to the inherent quality of the image. The density of haze is subject to considerable variation, and as a result, extant dehazing algorithms frequently struggle to effectively manage differing haze densities. This often culminates in issues such as color distortion, loss of detail, and the emergence of other artifacts. In response to these challenges, this study introduces an innovative adaptive image dehazing algorithm. This algorithm employs a Generative Adversarial Network (GAN) as its foundational structure. Furthermore, an attention mechanism is integrated into the algorithm with the aim of preventing detail loss and concentrating on salient feature information. The proposed algorithm is subjected to rigorous evaluation across diverse datasets. The results demonstrate that it surpasses existing methods in terms of both image quality and robustness in relation to varying haze densities.

articleTitle: A multi-scale feature pyramid fusion network for predicting the driver's visual attention
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Traffic driving scenarios are sophisticated and varied. Experienced drivers routinely allocate visual attention to critical targets and areas in advance and judge their intentions to ensure driving safety. Consequently, the research on the driver's visual attention allocation behavior is essential for the development of assisted driving systems and self-driving. Data-driven visual attention research has largely profited from the development of Convolutional Neural Networks in recent years. In this paper, we present a novel model that predicts accurate visual attention maps through the construction of a deep neural network, the integration of multiscale pyramid features, and the incorporation of neural attention mechanisms. Finally, extensive experimental evaluations indicate that the proposed model outperforms classical models and several excellent deep learning-based approaches on the TDV dataset.

articleTitle: Dermatoscopic Image Texture Features for Assessment of Skin Barrier
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Due to the increasing prevalence of sensitive skin, it is crucial to effectively evaluate the skin barrier function. As the gold standard for assessing the skin barrier, Transepidermal Water Loss (TEWL) has been limited in its widespread use due to its high measurement costs and stringent environmental requirements. This study proposes dermatoscopic image texture features for the assessment of the sensitive skin barrier, Specifically, we extracted Gray Level Co-occurrence Matrix (GLCM) and Local Binary Pattern (LBP) features after pre-processing the collected dermatoscopic images, which are expected to replace TEWL. Experimental results from model mice indicate a correlation between these texture features and TEWL values, suggesting that they can be regarded as effective indicators for assessing the barrier function of sensitive skin.

articleTitle: A new transformer-based axis temperature alarm system
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: The current axis temperature alarm system mainly determines the current alarm level based on the axle temperature status or characteristics detected by a single monitoring station, which has a problem: the characteristic data detected by the monitoring station is not related to the previously detected characteristic data. In this study, temperature rise, column temperature rise difference and vehicle temperature rise difference are taken as the feature data, and the attention mechanism model with mask is used to judge the current alarm level by combining the feature data measured by the previous monitoring station. The simulation results show that the optimized system has a discrimination agreement rate of 87.2% for the alarm level, which is a 13.5% increase in accuracy over the previous method.

articleTitle: Mesh Model Codec Based on Fusion Graph Convolution and Parallel Pooling
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Three-dimensional shape generation is an important research direction of computer graphics. In this paper, a graph convolutional neural network is introduced to obtain local features for a three-dimensional mesh model data set with the same connectivity relationship. A parallel pooling function is proposed to jointly extract richer global features, improve network generation performance, and ensure the robustness of the model during network training. Experiments are carried out on datasets such as Swing. The experimental results show that the mesh model codec network based on fusion graph convolution and parallel pooling proposed in this paper can effectively obtain global and local features in grid data and achieve a higher-quality mesh generation effect.

articleTitle: Recognition for Hybrid Modulation Based on Convolutional Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Hybrid modulation has attracted much attention because of its superior performance. However, its automatic modulation recognition (AMR) remains difficulties and gaps. To overcome the drawbacks of this issue, this paper focuses on the signal model and the external features of composite modulation types including FM-BPSK, FM-QPSK, FM-8PSK and FM-2FSK. A convolutional neural network (CNN) with signal phase as the input of the network is adopted to realize the classification. The proposed algorithm makes full use of powerful presentation ability of CNN. In this scheme, a lot of experiments have been down to validate that the proposed method is feasible and practicable.

articleTitle: Anomaly Transformer for Vibration Data Analysis: Case Study on CWRU Dataset
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Time series anomaly detection has a wide range of applications in various fields of society, one of which is the detection of anomalies in vibration data. Abnormal vibration data often indicates the existence of potential disasters or abnormal operation of equipment, so timely detection and identification is important for the prevention of earthquakes and improvement of industrial production efficiency. In this paper, an unsupervised time series anomaly detection algorithm, Anomaly Transformer, is used to detect anomalies in CWRU vibration datasets.Anomaly Transformer leverages the powerful characterization capabilities of the Transformer network and an improved anomaly attention mechanism to capture anomalies in the time series. Experimental results show that Anomaly Transformer exhibits excellent performance in the CWRU vibration dataset, achieving high precision and recall. In addition, Anomaly Transformer demonstrated a low false alarm rate, indicating its high accuracy in recognizing real anomalies. Future research can further explore the application of Anomaly Transformer in other domains with deeper optimization and extensions.

articleTitle: Screening method for automotive suspension parts based on image 3D reconstruction technology
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: To address screening suspension spring and lateral stabilizer bar inefficiencies, a screening method for 3D modeling based on 2D images is proposed. This replaces the previous manual inspection or scanner-based 3D model reconstruction. The first step is to set up the drive and camera array to capture 2D images of the processed parts from multiple angles. Then the SFM and MVS algorithms are used to obtain the 3D model of the part through a series of steps such as feature point extraction and matching, sparse reconstruction, global optimization of the beam method, and dense reconstruction. Eventually, after measuring and comparing the modeling results, the purpose of distinguishing the advantages and disadvantages is achieved. Compared to traditional screening methods, the modeling results based on 2D image reconstruction meet the accuracy requirements of the screened parts needed for the assembly line. It also effectively improves screening efficiency and shortens the work cycle.

articleTitle: A Review of Multi-View Clustering Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: With the rapid development of big data and the Internet of Things technology, people have easier access to data, which leads to different perspectives when observing data. As a result, multi-view data has emerged, which can effectively demonstrate different manifestations of a sample, but is often more complex to process. Multi-view clustering has received increasing attention in recent years, utilizing the consistency and complementarity among multiple views to conduct more effective digital representation, in order to obtain information that cannot be obtained from a single view and improve clustering effectiveness. This article provides a classification and detailed discussion of existing multi-view clustering methods, and summarizes current challenges and future development trends.

articleTitle: Sea Surface Small Target Detection Method Based on Improved YOLOv5
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: At present, a complete and feasible detection system for sea surface targets has not yet been formed. Weak and small targets appear more frequently in sea scenes, and there is a lack of targeted algorithms to achieve better detection and identification. Therefore, this paper proposes a sea surface small target detection method based on improved YOLOv5. First, a data set of small targets on the sea surface is constructed, and the YOLOv5 model is selected to achieve target detection; then the sea antenna detection algorithm, attention module SE, CBAM, CA, feature fusion module BiFPN, and loss function EIoU are used to optimize the data, model, and strategy respectively. Finally, model training and verification testing are carried out. Experimental results show that compared with the baseline model (YOLOv5), the improved YOLOv5-sea-sky-line model has improved precision, recall, and average precision by 2.8%, 1.6%, and 0.8% respectively.

articleTitle: Research on the farthest scattering distance of blasting flying stones based on improved WOA-BP neural network
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: The flying rocks in mining blasting operations pose a great threat to safety production, and the reasonable division of safety blasting scope is of great significance for production operations. In response to the problem of the farthest scattering distance of flying rocks in mining blasting operations, based on the excellent nonlinear mapping ability of BP neural network and mature research on its theory and application, WOA (whale optimization algorithm) is used to optimize the BP neural network, improving its weak global search ability and poor anti-interference ability. And adaptive weight adjustment is introduced, and an improved WOA-BP neural network model is applied to predict the farthest scattering distance of flying rocks in mining blasting. The minimum burden of blasting, unit consumption of blasting explosives, and maxi-mum charge weight of a single hole, which have a greater impact on the distance of flying rocks during blasting operation, are selected as input variables. The experimental results show that the average absolute error MAE, mean square error MSE, root mean square error RMSE, and average absolute percentage error MAPE of the improved WOA-BP model are 0.52283, 0.60303, 0.77655, and 2.8102%, respectively, which are better than the comparison model, indicating that the prediction accuracy of the model is high, it can provide guidance for actual mine blasting production.

articleTitle: Novel View Synthesis from a Single RGBD Image for Indoor Scenes
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: In this paper, we propose an approach for synthesizing novel view images from a single RGBD (Red Green Blue-Depth) input. Novel view synthesis (NVS) is an interesting computer vision task with extensive applications. Methods using multiple images has been well-studied, exemplary ones include training scene-specific Neural Radiance Fields (NeRF), or leveraging multi-view stereo (MVS) and 3D rendering pipelines. However, both are either computationally intensive or non-generalizable across different scenes, limiting their practical value. Conversely, the depth information embedded in RGBD images unlocks 3D potential from a singular view, simplifying NVS. The widespread availability of compact, affordable stereo cameras, and even LiDARs in contemporary devices like smartphones, makes capturing RGBD images more accessible than ever. In our method, we convert an RGBD image into a point cloud and render it from a different viewpoint, then formulate the NVS task into an image translation problem. We leveraged generative adversarial networks to style-transfer the rendered image, achieving a result similar to a photograph taken from the new perspective. We explore both unsupervised learning using CycleGAN and supervised learning with Pix2Pix, and demonstrate the qualitative results. Our method circumvents the limitations of traditional multi-image techniques, holding significant promise for practical, real-time applications in NVS.

articleTitle: Research on Warehouse Object Detection for Mobile Robot Based on YOLOv5
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: In view of the lack of public datasets for object detection in warehouse environment, a large number of images containing cargos, trays and forklifts in real warehouse environment is collected and annotated by cameras, creating a warehouse object dataset. At the same time, in view of the low detection accuracy of traditional object detection algorithms in warehouse environment, the YOLOv5 series models are applied to warehouse environment, and the models are trained and optimized on the warehouse object dataset created by ourselves, achieving accurate detection of warehouse object. The mAP@50 of the YOLOv5 series models has reached more than 99%. Among them, the mAP@50-90 of the YOLOv5l model and YOLOv5x model is about 92%, which is better than other models. The YOLOv5m model is also deployed on the self-designed mobile robot, realizing the automatic detection of warehouse object. The experimental results show that YOLOv5m has achieved a satisfactory warehouse object detection effect, and it has certain practical value in the field of warehouse object detection.

articleTitle: Research on Infrared Nonuniformity Correction Method Based on Transformer
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Aiming at the problems of low generalization ability and high system complexity in the existing infrared image nonuniformity correction methods, this paper proposes a single-frame infrared image nonuniformity correction method based on Transformer, which has the advantages of simple network structure, strong model generalization ability, etc., and the average residual nonuniformity of the images in the test set can reach below 5%.

articleTitle: Density Peaks Clustering Algorithm Based on Two-step Allocation Strategy
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Density peaks clustering is a simple and efficient density-based clustering algorithm and has attracted wide attention in recent years. However, due to the lack of error correction, the one-step allocation strategy for typical density peaks clustering tends to cause the Domino effect. To solve this problem, this paper proposes a density peaks clustering algorithm based on a two-step allocation strategy. According to the original one-step allocation strategy, we first assign labels to all points. In the first step, we assign the trusted label or the pending label, whether the information of the point and its K-nearest neighbors is consistent, to each point. In the second step, we focus on the trusted labels of the K-nearest neighbors to correct the remaining points with pending labels. Finally, the density peaks clustering algorithm based on the two-step allocation strategy achieves excellent clustering performances on benchmark datasets. The code can be downloaded from https://github.com/Gedanke/DPC-TAS.

articleTitle: Research on gridded UAV scheduling based on heuristic greedy algorithm
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Traditional UAV scheduling algorithm has the problem of low search efficiency and easy to fall into the local optimum. Firstly, this paper assumes that a single receiving signal UAV is regulated by three launch signal drones. The positions of the fixed launch signal drones are given at (100,0),(0,0) and (0,100).Grid the receiver deviation domain. To achieve the scheduling visualization, set a single step length in 8 directions in 45°, 30 steps in a single iteration cycle. Secondly, to validate that the probability-based heuristic greedy algorithm has stronger search efficiency, this paper studies the application effect of traditional greedy algorithm, heuristic greedy algorithm and probability-based heuristic greedy algorithm in UAV scheduling from the actual deviation position to the ideal position. Finally, after 5,000 iterations, the scheduling average error can be reduced from 1.56° to 0.3°, it provides a new algorithm idea for the UAV to realize accurate scheduling.

articleTitle: Image Monitoring System Based on Deep Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: For safety and security reasons, the indoor/outdoor working environments of various industries require the use of many cameras for automated surveillance. In such context, a major challenge for automated monitoring system is achieving high-precision real-time performance for image classification and object detection. In this paper, we present a novel image surveillance system based on a combined approach derived from YOLO V5. The system first detects moving targets using background subtraction. Then, we propose a modified YOLO V5 algorithm for accurately detecting and categorizing different objects in images captured in a video stream. The system runs in real time and could analyze multiple video streams simultaneously. The results of the experiments show that this system has good performance and could be widely applied on several areas, such as security, surveillance, and traffic management.

articleTitle: Spaceborne SAR Ship Data Expansion Based on GAN
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: In response to the lack of high-quality and sufficient synthetic aperture radar (SAR) data that can be paired with light ship images in practice, this paper proposes a method to convert optical ship images into SAR images based on GAN networks. In order to improve the coordination of generated images and stabilize the training process, this paper establishes a generator with a self-attention mechanism combined with spectral normalization operations. Secondly, the maximum spatial perturbation consistency loss is introduced to reduce the spatial changes between optical images and SAR images caused by changes in ship size and background noise. Finally, in order to speed up the convergence speed and stability of the model, a relative discriminator is introduced. Experiments conducted on the HRSID and LEVIR remote sensing ship data sets show that the FID (Fréchet Inception Distance) of the SAR ship images generated by this model is reduced to 57.25. At the same time, compared with the current optimal algorithm, the peak signal-to-noise ratio is increased by 5.89% on average. The structural similarity loss is increased by 18.75% on average, and the mean square error is reduced by 13.44% on average.

articleTitle: Multi-scale Self-similarity Network for Few-Shot Segmentation
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Few-shot segmentation is a specific type of segmentation in few-shot setting, using only a few number of annotated samples to segment unseen class objects in the given query samples. This challenging task faces the threats posed by large intra-class variations existing in support and query samples. To alleviate the inherent noise in matching relationship representation brought by intra-class variation, we present self-similarity representation by designing the multi-scale self-similarity module. It calculates the correspondence between the feature and its surrounding representation, which provides robustness for the network. Additionally, we further utilize the self-similarity representation by proposing the cross-attention decoder module to guide query feature in the decoding process. Comprehensive experiments on PASCAL-5i dataset in 1-shot and 5-shot paradigm demonstrate the superiority of our designed model. Our designed model significantly improves segmentation performance with only a few more expenses of training parameters.

articleTitle: Boosting Image Classification Accuracy Leveraging Finer Grained Labels
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: As the landscape of deep learning has evolved rapidly, numerous models and methodologies have emerged, revolutionizing the domain of image classification. In recent years, OpenAI’s Contrastive Language-Image Pre-Training (CLIP) model, which uniquely bridges visual and textual information, has demonstrated robust generalization across diverse tasks, presenting fresh avenues and opportunities for image classification. Building upon the capabilities of the CLIP model, this research further explores the possibility that finer grained labels may help improve the accuracy of image classification. The proposed method is divided into three steps. First, determine existing or manually annotated sub-class labels to capture nuanced details within primary categories. Second, use CLIP as a feature extractor, augmented with a fully connected layer. This setup facilitates supervised classification, leveraging the granularity of the identified sub-class labels. Third, the classified sub-labels are mapped back to their parent categories, resulting in the final prediction. By introducing and combining the precision of finer-grained labels with CLIP’s robust architecture, this method offers a promising avenue for bolstering classification accuracy. Code is available at https://github.com/24kcqsn/Image-Classification-Leveraging-Finer-Grained-Labels

articleTitle: Advancing Quality and Detail: Enhanced-LapSRN for Chip Socket Image Super-Resolution
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Recently, image super-resolution reconstruction models based on deep neural networks have achieved remarkable success. This paper introduces a network named Enhanced-LapSRN, designed using the classic CNN structure. This network not only effectively utilizes the pyramid structure from the LapSRN to construct high-resolution image residuals but also incorporates the architectural concept of DenseNet to facilitate feature reuse and prevent information loss. Additionally, we employ dilated convolution and convolution cascade techniques to expand the receptive field and introduce a convolution block attention module(CBAM) to focus more on high-frequency information in the image. This allows for the comprehensive integration of image features at different levels and results in comprehensive feature extraction. Further experiments confirm the strong performance of our method on public datasets, with a notable 0.49dB improvement in SET5, as well as an 8\% enhancement in positioning accuracy on our self-constructed chip socket datasets. Furthermore, our method is capable of real-time processing, ensuring high efficiency.

articleTitle: Multiple Image Augmentations for Enhanced YOLO-based Traffic Sign Detection
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: The rapid growth of the automotive industry necessitates the implementation of robust passenger safety measures, especially in the domain of traffic sign recognition for autonomous driving. This study introduces an effective approach to enhance traffic sign detection, with a specific emphasis on the You Only Look Once (YOLO) architecture. The paper addresses the challenges associated with accurately localizing traffic signs by employing diverse image augmentation techniques, including flipping, color inversion, Gaussian blur, affine transformation, and brightness adjustment. Despite computational challenges, particularly in light of YOLOv5's superior accuracy and efficiency, there is still room for further refinement to meet the stringent requirements of autonomous driving research. This research underscores the potential of image augmentation in advancing traffic sign recognition, demonstrating its pivotal role in the development of intelligent transportation systems. In comparison to existing algorithms as YOLO-V3 and YOLO-V5, the proposed technique might successfully reach higher accuracy and less computational power and processing time.

articleTitle: Segmenting Sonar Images with an Enhanced OTSU Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Sonar image segmentation technique is crucial for underwater target tracking, among other things. Due to the undersea environment's influence, noise is easily absorbed, which leads to a poor tracking performance. In order to address the issues with the traditional one-dimensional and two-dimensional OTSU algorithms, which have a slow computation time and poor anti-noise performance, this paper proposes a fast OTSU segmentation algorithm based on wavelet boosting and analyses the algorithmic principles and implementation steps of one-dimensional OTSU algorithm, two-dimensional OTSU algorithm and its fast algorithm, fast algorithm with the variance as the eigenvalue, and maximum entropy algorithm. On the basis of this, the aforementioned algorithms are used to perform image segmentation on four photos. The segmentation findings demonstrate the method's quick processing speed and strong noise resistance, which have significant implications for sonar image segmentation applications.

articleTitle: Pre-Training For mmWave Radar Object Detection Through Masked Image Modeling
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Millimeter-wave (mmWave) radar object detection (ROD) is an indispensable technique in autonomous driving technology because of its ability to maintain stability in complex environments. Deep learning (DL) techniques have made promising achievements in radar target detection techniques, but these techniques usually require large labeled datasets. However, the labeling of millimeter-wave radar datasets is more complex. In this paper, we introduce a novel pre-training method based on mask image modeling (MIM) in the ROD task, aiming to address the dataset limitations in the development of ROD techniques. The method performs spatial and temporal masking operations on unlabeled millimeter-wave radar images, which can acquire more spatial and temporal features simultaneously in the pre-training stage. Furthermore, inspired by T-RODNet, this paper presents a lightweight SS-RODNet network for testing the effectiveness of the proposed MIM method. The model aims to fully integrate the advantages of extracting local and global features. Numerous ablation experiments prove that the proposed MIM method is effective, and SS-RODNet achieves second place on the CRUW datasets.

articleTitle: Research on face video generation algorithm based on speech content
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Aiming at the problem that the audio and lip motion are not synchronized and the face appears white light in the speech-driven face speech video, the audio-visual synchronization module and the highlight noise reduction module are proposed on the basis of the Wav2Lip network. Firstly, the sound visual alignment module is added to make the model learn the context information of the speech signal in the forward and backward directions, so as to improve the accuracy of lip synchronization. Secondly, in the image encoder, the highlight noise reduction module (HDM) is introduced to solve the problem of noise and overexposure in the highlight area of the generated speech face video. The experimental results on the LRS2 dataset show that the confidence score (LSE-C), the deviation index (LSE-D) and the image structure similarity (SSIM) of the audio-visual quality alignment network (AVQA) in this paper reach 8.565 and 4.605 and 0.872 respectively.

articleTitle: TransGait: Vision Transformer Based Gait Recognition Network
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Gait, the distinctive walking pattern of an individual, stands out as a human modality that can be effortlessly captured even with low-resolution cameras from a considerable distance. Gait patterns are unique to each individual and hard to fake. Gait recognition is a cutting-edge biometric technology that focuses on identifying individuals based on their distinctive walking patterns. Therefore, its fields of application span a number of domains, encompassing healthcare, robotics, automation, as well as security and access control. The origin of this investigation stems from challenges faced by high school and college residents contending with forgotten identification credentials, compounded by the intricacies of facial recognition in the context of the COVID-19 pandemic, especially in instances involving mask-obscured facial features. This paper proposes Transformer based Gait Recognition Network (Occlusion-TransGait), which combining temporal Vision Transformer (VIT) and Swin Transformer based structure and occlusion masked datasets. Utilizing the Swin Transformer model, the study achieved enhanced precision, with improvements of 0.4% for NM, 1.0% for BG, and 1.4% for CL. Furthermore, this paper presents a novel open-set detection technique for recognizing potential threats arising from unidentified individuals. Finally, this research embraces an inventive strategy that integrates human detection, tracking, and segmentation to create an end-to-end pipeline well-suited for implementation on the NVIDIA Jetson platform. This research promises a transformative impact on gait recognition systems, enhancing their effectiveness and security, and paving the way for stronger and more efficient biometric solutions.

articleTitle: A high quality low-light image enhancement method
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Factors such as insufficient lighting, backlighting, and failed focusing can lead to low brightness, poor contrast, and noise in the collected images. These issues seriously affect the further analysis and processing of images, especially for color images with more information, which often result in color distortion after enhancement. In order to improve the quality of low light color images, this paper proposes a high-quality low light color image enhancement method. According to Retinex theory, the attention map and reflection map are initialized by constructing weight functions for three color channels, and used as inputs to the network. At the same time, using a dual discriminator structure and attention mechanism, an enhanced image is generated to achieve clearer image enhancement effects. Experimental results show that the method proposed in this paper can improve the quality of low light images with higher quality and effectiveness compared to mainstream enhancement algorithms.

articleTitle: Deblurring QR Code Images using Local Maximum and Minimum Intensity Prior
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: We propose a robust and fast QR code deblurring method using local maximum and minimum intensity (LMMI). The motivation for this work stems from a common characteristic observed during the image blur degradation process: the local maximum intensity tends to decrease, while the local minimum intensity tends to increase. This characteristic can be effectively utilized in the deblurring process of QR code images. Our algorithm binarized LMMI through a simple thresholding step, which improved the computational efficiency compared with the semi-quadratic splitting algorithm. The latent image estimation and kernel estimation are alternately solved within the maximum a posteriori framework until convergence. Experimental results show that our method significantly improves both deblurring effect and computational efficiency.

articleTitle: An improved lightweight segmentation neural network for dermoscopic lesion images based on knowledge distillation
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: As artificial intelligence technology rapidly advances, numerous medical image segmentation models based on deep learning have been developed. However, the current mainstream neural network algorithms usually have too many parameters, complex models, and high computational complexity. To better facilitate the operation of neural networks on low-power devices while preserving model segmentation precision, this paper introduces an enhanced lightweight segmentation neural network for dermoscopic lesion images, LDLSNet (Lightweight Dermoscopic Lesion Segmentation Net), by redesigning the network structure and employing advanced attention mechanisms. The model’s parameter count is reduced via knowledge distillation. LDLSNet can address the limitations of current skin lesion images segmentation techniques and offers a more lightweight approach to segmentation. This paper elaborates on the architecture and learning methodology of the suggested LDLSNet model and carries out experimental substantiation using the ISIC dataset. Experimental results indicate that while maintaining superior performance in dermoscopic lesion images segmentation tasks, the proposed method possesses fewer network parameters. This research offers a novel and effective solution in the field of lightweight dermoscopic lesion images segmentation, holding certain theoretical and practical implications.

articleTitle: Memory-Enhanced Sequential Variational Transformer for Inferring Neural Population Dynamics
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: As deep learning continues to expand its applications in neuroscience, studies on the dynamics of neural populations such as LFADS seek to infer the latent factors from the high-dimensional sequential features. However, these methods neglect the effects of the historical states on the current states of neurons. Therefore, we propose an innovative memory enhanced sequential variational transformer (MESVT), which combines the current states of neural population features with the historical states through the cross-attention mechanism. Furthermore, we validate the performance of MESVT on two collected single-cell-level recording datasets. Utilizing MESVT, we analyze the potential dynamic encoding mechanism of neural populations in the VISP (Ventrolateral Intraparietal Sulcus) for visual stimuli.

articleTitle: An Efficiency Framework for Task Allocation Based on Reinforcement Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: In response to the challenges of task allocation for Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) in large-scale scenarios, this paper proposes an improved task allocation method based on Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) algorithm and reinforcement learning, named PSO-DQN. We first design an innovational clustering method based on the K-Means algorithm, which combines the target importance with distance to reduce the computation complexity. The PSO-DQN method we formulated serves to allocate targets from UAV swarms to specific target clusters while simultaneously mapping individual targets within a cluster to UAVs. The experimental results demonstrate that the superior task allocation accuracy of the PSO-DQN method when compared to traditional approaches. The framework we proposed also proves that it can significantly reduce the complexity of computation of task allocation for UAV swarms in large-scale scenarios.

articleTitle: Enhanced Remote Sensing Object Detection Algorithm Based on YOLOv7
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Remote sensing object detection faces challenges such as densely distributed objects, complex backgrounds, and significant variations in object scale, which result in issues like missed detections and false positives. Additionally, the detection process suffers from long-range dependencies, leading to the loss of detailed spatial semantic information. In this study, we present an enhanced YOLOv7-based algorithm for remote sensing object detection. Initially, deformable convolution layers, specifically Dynamic Convolution (ODConv), are incorporated to bolster the network's feature extraction capabilities. Subsequently, the ELAN module is improved through the implementation of the SimAM attention mechanism, mitigating to some extent the issues of long-range dependencies and the resultant false positives and negatives caused by complex backgrounds and dense object distributions. Finally, the original loss function is optimized using an EIOU loss function, thereby improving the network's localization accuracy and accelerating model convergence. On the DOTA dataset, the modified algorithm achieves a mean average precision (mAP) of 0.5 at 67.5%, representing a 4.9% improvement compared to the original YOLOv7 model.

articleTitle: Metric-based few-shot learning method for driver distracted behaviors detection
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Traditional supervised learning method meets problems such as difficulty in data collection and labeling when applied in special tasks such as driver distracted behaviors detection. Classic Prototype Networks are proposed to solve these few-shot learning problems. However, the fixed prototype representation of the Prototype Network makes its detection accuracy susceptible to the influence of support set samples, making it difficult to apply stably. Therefore, we propose a method to obtain adaptive dynamic prototype representation, and introduce a distance scaling loss function to optimize the training of the network, so that the network can be optimized in the direction of shortening the intra-class distance and enlarging the inter-classes distance. Experiments show that the accuracy of our proposed method in the driver distracted behaviors detection dataset Drive&Act is improved by 3.13% compared to the prototype network, and 9.15% improved compared to traditional supervised learning.

articleTitle: High-Resolution Range Profile Recognition of Midcourse Ballistic Targets Based on AMTrans
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: To address the problem of high-precision time-series recognition of high-resolution range profiles (HRRP) of ballistic midcourse targets, we propose a HRRP recognition method based on the multivariate time-series learning approach of Transformer encoder to further improve the recognition efficiency and accuracy. The AMTrans model is based on a multi-headed attention mechanism which can take into account multiple correlations among the input elements and adaptively adjust the attention weight in different distance units. The experimental results show that this proposed method has significant performance advantages over other methods and has better robustness.

Author Keywords: recognition of midcourse ballistic missile target

articleTitle: Adaptive Feature Calibration Siamese Network for Rotating Object Tracking
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: The Siamese-based object tracking algorithms employ random angle embedding to mitigate accuracy degradation caused by object rotation. However, it only adds prior knowledge as predefined patterns without alleviating the feature misalignment and local equivariance caused by rotation. In this paper, we propose a Siamese network with feature-calibration (AFC-Siam Net), which establishes the spatial correspondence relationship of the misalignment features for the same object under different rotation angles by dual-templates input structure with an affine transformation filter. Compared to existing Siamese-based trackers, AFC-Siam Net calibrates the features without the need for carefully designed prior knowledge. The experimental results confirm the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm through comprehensive evaluations on widely adopted datasets in the field of visual object tracking.

articleTitle: Prediction of praseodymium/neodymium multicomponent content based on IHHO-ELM
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: In order to solve the current situation that it is difficult to detect praseodymium/neodymium elements in rare earth mixed solutions in real time, a multicomponent content prediction method for praseodymium/neodymium elements based on IHHO-ELM is proposed. Tent mapping and reverse learning strategy are introduced in the initialisation stage of the population, and the parameters such as weights and thresholds of the limit learning machine are selected using the improved HHO algorithm, which retains the algorithm’s optimization seeking mechanism and improves the convergence speed on the basis of improving the algorithm’s performance. Meanwhile, the simulation simulation experiments are carried out with the images of praseodymium/neodymium two rare earth extraction solutions possessing ionic colour characteristics as an example, and the experimental data are obtained and then compared and analysed. The analysed results show that the method proposed in this paper can effectively reduce the measurement error and has high prediction accuracy and stability, which has certain theoretical significance and practical value for the rare earth extraction industry.

articleTitle: Hardware and Software Co-Design Approach for Background Subtraction in High-Resolution Videos
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Full High-Definition video has become the predominant resolution for surveillance cameras. However, the real-time background subtraction methods on Internet of Things (IoT) edge devices remain a challenge. In this paper, we propose a hardware and software co-design approach for high-resolution video background subtraction based on an improved Content Adaptive Resizing Framework (CARF) method. We retain the core of the CARF algorithm, which preserves object boundary information by coupling downsampling and upsampling layers. To reduce the algorithm’s demands on hardware resources, we have made specific modifications to CARF for the background subtraction task. These modifications include incorporating edge detection algorithms to retain boundary pixels and ignore non boundary redundant pixels, as well as fine-tuning the algorithm’s details. The modified algorithm performs nearly as well as the original one but requires fewer resources, making it more suitable for hardware implementation. The entire method is implemented on the Xilinx Zynq MPSoC, utilizing the programmable logic (PL) for hardware acceleration of this framework and the processing system (PS) for background subtraction. We validate the real-time performance of the proposed method on 1080p resolution datasets and analyze resource usage.

articleTitle: Fast Video Watermarking Scheme Based on Adaptive Tensor Block Selection
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: The traditional watermarking method regards the video as a series of video frames, and carries out the same watermark embedding operation for each frame, without considering the temporal correlation between video frames. The traditional method is always based on embedding watermark in a fixed number of frames, without considering the relationship between the contents of video segments, which has high computational complexity and large memory consumption. Therefore, we propose a video watermarking algorithm based on fast selection of embedded blocks. Firstly, we use AKAZE feature points and mean square error to segment the video adaptively, and then select the texture block as the video block to embed the watermark based on the feature block, and realize the watermark embedding by quantifying the core tensor. Experiments show that the algorithm not only improves the speed, but also has strong robustness to various attacks.

articleTitle: Detection and Segmentation of Grape Bunch by Integrating Channel Attention and Large Kernel Attention
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Detecting and segmenting fruits in an orchard environment is a vital technique in multiple applications of precision agriculture, such as automated harvesting and yield estimation. This study aims to improve the accuracy and robustness of detectors for detecting and segmenting fruits on trees by integrating detection and segmentation models based on channel and large kernel attention. The proposed Triplet-Large Kernel Attention (TLKA) module inherits the advantages of channel and large kernel attention. It was integrated with YOLOv7 to achieve real-time object detection and segmentation. Several experiments were conducted to verify the effectiveness of the proposed TLKA module. These included comparative attention mechanisms from small to large input image scales, comparative analysis of different attention mechanisms through Grad-CAM visualization, and test experiments with integrated comparisons on mid-term fruits (immature, intermediate, and mature) under three different light conditions (morning, noon, and afternoon). The proposed TLKA module achieved higher accuracy than comparative attention at different input scales. Finally, the proposed model was used to predict the yield of both grapes. The TLKA-YOLOv7 outperformed all other investigated models in terms of grape bunch detection and segmentation and obtained more competitive results in yield prediction.

articleTitle: A solar irradiance prediction method based on signal decomposition and Informer
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: The historical data of solar irradiance are characterized by volatility and instability. These characteristics make it difficult to obtain satisfactory results when directly using prediction models to predict solar irradiance data. Therefore, this paper proposes a solar irradiance prediction model that combines signal decomposition methods and deep learning methods. First, feature selection is performed on the collected various meteorological characteristic data to determine the meteorological characteristics used for prediction. Secondly, in order to reduce the error in prediction results caused by the complexity of solar irradiance data, this method uses variational mode decomposition (VMD) to decompose the original data into multiple relatively stable subsequences. Thirdly, multiple sequences are predicted separately through the Informer model, and finally the prediction results are superimposed to obtain the final prediction value. Experiments show that the VMD-Informer model has higher accuracy in solar irradiance prediction than common deep learning models.

articleTitle: FATA3D: 3D-aware Talking Face Animation via Tri-plane Alignment
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Generating multi-view consistent talking head videos from a single facial image and corresponding spoken audio is a challenging task. On one hand, it often results in facial expressions that do not match the speech, and the head movement between frames can appear unnatural. On the other hand, ensuring 3D consistency is difficult due to the lack of multi-view references. Addressing these challenges, we propose FATA3D, a method that leverages 3D-aware generative priors. Specifically, for 3D consistency, we depart from previous approaches by using a nerf-based volume renderer, combined with pretrained weights trained on extensive data. By harnessing this powerful 3D prior, we successfully overcome this challenge. To address the issues related to expressions and head poses, we introduce expression residual alignment and head pose alignment. These networks effectively bridge the gap between audio signals and facial pose and expression changes. The outputs of these modules are used to enhance the input features of the renderer, resulting in improved and coherent animations. Our experiments show that compared to existing methods, our approach produces more faithful animation.

articleTitle: Nighttime Haze Image Restoration using Rolling Guidance Filter
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Nighttime haze removal techniques are crucial to enhancing the visibility of hazy nighttime scenes, which often suffer from low light, intense glow, light scattering, and multicolored light sources. Existing daytime dehazing methods may not be suitable for nighttime images due to the spatially non-uniform environmental illumination, resulting in difficulties in addressing glow or low-light conditions. Therefore, developing techniques to effectively remove nighttime haze remains a challenging task. In this paper, we propose a Nighttime image Dehazing algorithm based on Rolling Guidance Filter, called NDRGF. Recognizing the typically non-uniform illumination in nighttime images, we initially employ a homomorphic filter to enhance the under-illuminated areas. Subsequently, given the inevitable noise in nighttime images, we apply a rolling guidance filter to suppress noise while preserving the structural information of the image. After that, we remove haze according to the conventional atmospheric scattering model. To solve this model, we introduce a local maximum brightness-based atmospheric light estimation algorithm, which divides the input image into patches using a fixed-size window. Within each local patch, the RGB value of the pixels exhibiting the maximum brightness is employed as the atmospheric light for the current region. In addition, we propose a simple and effective algorithm for transmission estimation utilizing a pixel-wise dark channel strategy, followed by a rolling guidance filter to smooth the texture in the transmission map while preserving salient geometric structures, thus yielding a reasonable transmission map. Quantitative and qualitative experiments tested on real-world and synthetic images corroborate the superior dehazing performance of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: Large Kernel Convolutional Neural Networks for Action Recognition Based on RepLKNet
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: To improve the classification accuracy of human actions in videos, two algorithms based on RepLKNet, a large kernel neural network, are proposed. By combining RepLKNet with Temporal Segment Networks (TSN) and incorporating the Temporal Shift Module (TSM), the models can better extract spatiotemporal information from videos, leading to improved classification accuracy. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed models achieve higher classification accuracy compared to previous convolutional neural network (CNN) models. Moreover, these models outperform transformer-based models such as TimeSformer in classification accuracy while requiring significantly fewer parameters.

articleTitle: Image classification of electronic components based on Vision Transformer
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Image recognition of electronic components is an important application field, which can be applied to the detection, identification and sequencing of electronic components. In order to solve the problem of electronic component recognition, an image recognition algorithm based on Vision Transformer (ViT) is proposed. Traditional image recognition algorithms of electronic components usually use convolutional neural networks, but there are some problems such as long training time and the need to master the global information. During the experiment, transfer learning method and data-enhanced image preprocessing method are used to improve the performance and robustness of the classification network, and the classification accuracy and recognition speed of Vision Transformer and traditional convolutional neural network in the classification task of electronic components are tested and compared. The test results show that compared with traditional convolutional neural networks, Vision Transformer's self-attention mechanism is more efficient for feature extraction, and the highest recognition accuracy in electronic component image classification tasks can reach 98.4%. In the classification task of small and medium-sized data sets, the Vision Transformer network self-attention structure can achieve the same recognition accuracy as the lightweight convolutional neural network ResNet-50, while significantly improving the training speed and classification speed.

Author Keywords: the image classification of electronic components

articleTitle: A 3D object detection strategy based on YOLOv8 combined with CaDDN for vehicle images
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: With the rapid development of deep learning and computer vision technologies, 3D object detection has become more and more widely used in fields such as autonomous driving, robotics and augmented reality. However, 3D object detection from monocular images is still a challenging problem. To solve this problem, this paper proposes a new method combining YOLOv8 and CaDDN (abbreviated as YO-Ca). First, we use YOLOv8 to perform 2D object category detection on monocular images, providing a 2D bounding box for each detected vehicle. Then, we employ the linear increasing discretization (LID) approach in the CaDDN method to predict the depth distribution of each pixel. In this way, we can accurately localize the image information in 3D space. Then, we convert the 2D bounding box into a 3D bounding box in the bird's-eye view, and refine and verify the 3D bounding box in the bird's-eye view. The experimental results show that our proposed YO-Ca method achieves better performance on the KITTI dataset, especially in terms of 3D intersection and merger ratio (IoU=0.7).

articleTitle: Multi-scale Feature Modification Network for FewShot Image Classification
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Few-shot image classification aims to learn a model that can adopt to unseen classes with few labeled data. This challenging problem requires to overcome the distribution shift of features due to differences between the novel classes and the base classes. Inspired by transformer style self-attention mechanism and feature pyramid, we propose a multi-scale cross-attention module. This module enables the correction of features by interacting with feature information at different scales and obtains the feature set of the sample. In addition, from the perspective of metric learning, we further propose a distance metric module to measure the distance between sets of features, thus better characterizing the similarity between samples. Extensive experiments on two public benchmarks in both 1-shot and 5-shot setting demonstrate the effectiveness of our method, which is a significant performance improvement over most methods.

articleTitle: Adaptive Facial Landmark Detection Algorithm Based on Supervised Learning
