abstract: Industrial safety is essential for the reliability and sustainability of production operations. In this study, a safety protective equipment detection scheme based on YOLOv8 algorithm is proposed for industrial security scenarios. By optimizing the lightweight strategy and updating the weight of the original YOLOv8 model, a more efficient network architecture is adopted, which reduces the complexity of the model while ensuring detection accuracy, and deploys the lightweight model on edge applications. Experimental results show that the optimized lightweight model achieves 94% of the mAP50 values on the detection tasks of four types of safety protective equipment, and can be monitored in real time at a speed of 17 frames per second, achieving a good balance between accuracy and efficiency. This study provides a low-complexity, high-efficiency intelligent detection system scheme for industrial safety monitoring.

articleTitle: Entity Linking Supported Multimodal Data: Fusing Text and Image features for Higher Accuracy
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: To address the problem of the low accuracy of traditional text-only data entity linking methods, this paper proposes a new multimodal entity-linking model that leverages the richness and complementarity of multi-modal information by effectively integrating text and image characteristics to enhance the accuracy of entity linking. The proposed method uses Bert model and the CNN-RNN model to stratify the image and text characteristics that contain the references, respectively; then the mechanism of co-attention and the method of gate fusion are imported to learn the correlation between text and images automatically; and the weight and importance of the characteristics are adjusted to achieve accurate alignment and interaction between the text and the images. Finally, the cosine similarity are used to measure the similarities between the candidate entities and mentions. Furthermore, experimental research is proposed with the RMEL and WMEL Multimodal Entity Linking Dataset.The results show that the proposed method outperforms other entity-linked models.

articleTitle: MATLAB-based regional live-action aerial video animation
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Image acts as a carrier of information, people began to study the image processing technology in order to improve the efficiency of screening information, Image processing can take advantage of powerful matrix labs (MATLAB).In daily work and life, it is mostly seen to use unmanned aerial vehicle for aerial photography and delivery of information. This design uses Dajiang Drone drones for regional aerial photography in terms of hardware. The aerial video is processed using Matrix Lab (MATLAB). Firstly, the dynamic video is written to the system as frame-by-frame still pictures by frame-by-frame digitization. Secondly, the video is written as frame pictures, and then each photo is animated using the filter function. Finally, all the processed frame-by-frame pictures and then re-written into the video to achieve the animation processing effect.

articleTitle: Research on image retrieval based on artificial intelligence technology
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Image retrieval holds significant importance within the realm of computer vision. This paper introduces SCDNet, a novel network model, leveraging selected feature aggregation for enhanced image retrieval. Using Thangka images as an illustrative example, the proposed model aims to address issues such as inadequate semantic feature extraction and image feature distortions due to background or noise. SCDNet firstly uses VGG16 network to extract semantic features from different convolutional layers of Thangka images, then passes through feature screening module, feature aggregation module, and rearrangement module, thereby completing the retrieval. Our experimental validation on homemade Thangka image dataset and publicly available fine-grained image dataset, demonstrating the superiority of SCDNet compared with other retrieval algorithms.

articleTitle: Text-to-image approach combining information blending structure and attention
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: The semantic consistency, loss of detail features, and other problems are caused by the traditional text generation image method's focus on extracting the information transmitted by the previous layer while ignoring the information of the layer's features that are lost during the subsequent propagation process. Text-to-images combining information blending structure and attention (CAGAN) with information fusion capabilities is suggested in order to address the aforementioned issues. The word and sentence levels of the text's characteristics are encoded using the pre-trained BiLSTM model. The network structure includes a feature fusion module that receives upper-level transmission information while maintaining feature information at the same level. The resulting image's semantic coherence is enhanced, and the image's features are refined, thanks to the application of the affine transformation to map the visual features based on natural language descriptions. According to the experimental findings, the CAGAN's FID score in the CUB dataset is 15.93, and its IS index is 4.84±0.04 in the CUB dataset. It has been greatly improved when compared to the current standard AttGAN and DMGAN models, demonstrating the usefulness of the suggested network.

articleTitle: Research on Intelligent Noise Reduction Method for CT Images Based on Attention Mechanism
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: With the widespread use of computed tomography (CT) technology, the demand for high-quality CT images is increasing, and how to achieve efficient and high-quality image noise reduction has been a hot research topic in the field of CT. In this paper, we focus on the intelligent noise reduction method of CT images based on attention mechanism. In this paper, U-Net is selected as the base network, and the channel attention module and pixel attention module are chosen for the study. To further improve the performance of pixel attention, we propose to introduce multi-scale convolution and residual modules to optimize it. By adding the channel attention and the optimized pixel attention, a lightweight noise reduction network is proposed in this paper. Compared with CBDNet, this network is lighter and faster, and the peak signal-to-noise ratio of noise reduction results is improved by 0.14 dB on average and the model is more stable under the simulated dataset, and the structural similarity of noise reduction results is improved by 0.036% under the real sample dataset.

articleTitle: Distribution Adaptation and Discriminative Feature Learning for Unsupervised Domain Adaptation
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Unsupervised domain adaptation is a classification problem that uses labeled source domain to help unlabeled target domain achieve better classification results. The main approach to unsupervised domain adaptation is to make classifiers trained on the source domain and use on the target domain by reducing the domain discrepancy between the source and target domains. However, most of the current domain adaptation methods treat the marginal and conditional probability distribution equally, In practical applications, since the discrepancy between the source and target domains are various, it is necessary to dynamically adjust the weight parameters of the source and target domain adaptation. In this paper, we propose a method to dynamically adapt the probability distributions of source and target domains, and learn the class discriminative features in the adaptation process to constrain the distance between samples of the same category to be as small as possible and the distance between samples of different categories to be as large as possible in the shared common subspace, so that the original samples have better differentiability after the projection. A large number of experiments have conducted on several visual cross-domain classification tasks show that our algorithm behaves much better than the previous ones.

articleTitle: Maritime Ship Target Detection Based on the YOLOv7 Model
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Maritime ship target detection plays a significant role in the modern maritime domain. However, challenges such as low detection accuracy, false positives, and missed detections hinder its effectiveness due to the complexity of the maritime environment and the diversity and variability of ships. To address this challenge, we propose a sea ship target detection method based on YOLOv7. Firstly, we replace the main neural network with MobileNetv1, reducing model parameters and enhancing inference speed. Secondly, in the feature fusion section, we introduce a shallow feature fusion pathway to comprehensively capture image details and contextual information, improving the detection capability for objects of various scales. Experimental data demonstrates that the enhanced YOLOv7 model has achieved significant results, achieving an average precision of 97.16%, which represents a 5.53% improvement over the initial model. This validates the feasibility of our approach.

articleTitle: CNN-based On-board Intelligent Processing for Remote Sensing Images Interpretation
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Traditional remote sensing image processing is not able to provide timely information for near real-time applications due to the hysteresis of satellite-ground mutual communication and low processing efficiency. On-board intelligent processing is an important approach to improve the efficiency and intelligence of remote sensing satellites. This paper takes convolutional neural network (CNN) based on-board processing as the focus. Firstly, the basic workflow of CNN based on-board processing system is illustrated. Afterwards, the applications of lightweight CNN based on-board processing are thoroughly reviewed. The used CNN models are further analyzed to compare the advantages and disadvantages. Finally, current challenges are summarized and future works concerned with artificial intelligence are concluded.

articleTitle: 3D Human Motion Data Compression Based on Computer Vision
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: The motivation of this research is to address the issue of large storage and transmission space occupied by 3D human motion data, as well as the demand for large amounts of motion data in fields such as virtual reality and animation production. Our goal is to develop efficient 3D human motion data compression algorithms to reduce storage space and transmission bandwidth, while ensuring data quality and realism. The importance of 3D human motion data compression is mainly reflected in the fields of virtual reality and animation production. Virtual reality technology relies on accurate and realistic motion data, which often occupies a significant amount of space. Through effective compression algorithms, the storage space of motion data can be greatly reduced, thereby reducing hardware requirements and transmission costs, and improving the smoothness and real-time experience of virtual reality. In animation production, a large amount of motion data needs to be accurately captured and processed, and compression algorithms can optimize the storage and processing efficiency of the data, thereby improving the efficiency and quality of animation production. Through this research, we will delve into the technology and methods of 3D human motion data compression, and strive to provide a more efficient solution for compressing 3D human motion data with the help of advanced compression algorithms. This will bring many benefits to fields such as virtual reality and animation production, including cost reduction, performance improvement, and real-time capability, promoting innovation and development. In conclusion, this research will provide strong support and promotion for the compression of 3D human motion data and its application in virtual reality and animation production.

articleTitle: Training Spiking Neural Networks Using Randomness
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Artificial neural networks have demonstrated remarkable performance across many fields. However, their high training cost has led researchers to seek ways to reduce it. One promising alternative is spiking neural networks, which offer higher computational efficiency. Despite this advantage, spiking neural networks still lag behind artificial neural networks in accuracy. To address this issue, researchers have been focusing on how to train high-precision spiking neural networks. Unfortunately, this remains an unsolved problem in the field. This work proposes a new training idea that promotes the learning of more generalized features in spiking neural networks, and has been verified on the CIFAR10 and CIFAR100 datasets. By introducing randomness, spiking neural networks are able to achieve higher training accuracy. This work may propose new ideas for training spiking neural networks that could lead to more accurate and efficient models in the future.

articleTitle: Punisher: A Deep Reinforcement Learning Model Trained by Correcting Bad Actions
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) is a deep learning (DL) network model that uses environmental feedback to train and make decisions. Expected value, as a powerful mathematical tool, is widely used in DRL network training. However, there are often deviations between the expected values and the actual values obtained from the environment. Additionally, accumulative deviations are also present in DRL networks. The accumulation of these deviations can result in a slower training speed and negatively impact the network's stability. To address these issues, this paper proposes a new DRL training method called Punisher. The principle behind Punisher is to identify the bad actions made by the DRL agent and correct only those actions during the training process. By focusing on correcting the bad actions, Punisher aims to improve the overall performance and stability of the DRL network. The experimental results demonstrate that the Punisher method exhibits excellent performance, faster training speeds and greater network stability, making it a promising approach for efficiently training DRL agents in various applications. Experiments presented in the main content of this paper have been posted at GitHub at https://github.com/Jimmyoungyi/Punisher.

articleTitle: Garment collar recognition based on improved Mask RCNN network
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: As one of the essential components of clothing, the collar is a factor that people pay close attention to when selecting clothes, and it also affects the overall visual effect of clothes, so the classification and recognition of clothing collar styles has important practical value. In this paper, we use Mask RCNN, a widely used target detection algorithm in the field of deep learning, to classify and recognize clothing collar styles on the clothing collar style dataset we participated in the production of, and improve the network on this basis. Firstly, data enhancement is performed on the clothing collar styles dataset, which alleviates the overfitting problem to a certain extent, and also improves the accuracy and robustness of the model; ResNet50, the original feature extraction network, is replaced with ResNeXt101, which improves the ability of the network to extract features; FPN, the feature fusion network, is replaced with PAFPN, which alleviates the problem of ineffectiveness of detecting small targets; and the improvement of the In addition, the non-maximum suppression method (NMS) used in filtering candidate frames is improved to enhance the accuracy of target detection without affecting the computing speed. The experimental results show that compared with the primitive Mask RCNN, the improved algorithm has greater improvement in the tasks of clothing collar recognition and segmentation.

articleTitle: LED Color Quality Detection Technology Based on Image Processing
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Modern LED color quality detection systems (color calibration systems) often involve numerous color sensors and motors. Although this method has high detection accuracy, improper control of the motor can easily cause high-precision probes to collide with each other, causing unnecessary losses. In addition, if we want to further improve the utilization rate of calibration equipment, so that a machine can calibrate more light panels at the same time, relying solely on the increase in the number of motors and probes will lead to problems such as increased costs and reduced stability. If enough color information of LED can be collected through images and its quality can be successfully detected, it can get rid of the complex motor and color detection equipment, and even achieve the simultaneous detection of more lamp beads by one machine, thereby reducing detection costs. Therefore, this article combines image processing technology to first collect LED aperture color information, and then convert the color information into the HSL color space model for color quality analysis to determine whether the color quality is maintained within the allowable color difference range. This proves the possibility of using image processing technology to achieve LED color quality evaluation and provides theoretical support for further optimizing the color calibration system.

articleTitle: Visual Recognition Method of Road Sign Line Missing Based on Image High Resolution Reconstruction Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: The conventional visual identification method of road sign line loss mainly uses Sobel\Prewitt operator to dynamically divide the visual identification area, which is easily affected by the directional change of road signs, resulting in poor visual identification performance. Therefore, it is necessary to design a brand-new visual identification method of road sign line loss based on image high-resolution reconstruction algorithm. That is to say, the visual recognition features of road sign line missing are extracted, and the visual recognition algorithm of road sign line image super-resolution reconstruction is designed, thus realizing the visual recognition of road sign line missing. The experimental results show that the designed visual recognition method for high-resolution reconstruction of road marking line images has good recognition performance, accuracy and certain application value, and has made certain contributions to improving the safety of road traffic.

articleTitle: Learning a Residual Fusion Network for SAR Image Despeckling
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Deep convolutional neural networks (CNN) have recently been proven to be valid for synthetic aperture radar (SAR) image despeckling. However, these CNN-based despeckling algorithms do not make the most of multi-level features, especially high-frequency features, therefore achieving relatively poor performance. We develop a novel residual fusion model for SAR image depeckling (SAR-RFN). We make the most of multi-level features of different convolutional layers. To be specific, we design residual fusion block (RFB) to extract rich local features through dilated convolutions. Local feature fusion is used to combine all features and learn more effective local features. Moreover, The amalgamation of local features from all RFBs into global features is undertaken through global feature fusion to achieve holistic learning. Extensive experimentation illustrates the supremacy of our SAR-RFN over current leading-edge approaches regarding both quantitative and qualitative measures.

articleTitle: Research on single-pixel imaging reconstruction algorithm based on residual attention channel network
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Single-pixel imaging (SPI) refers to the complete image obtained by processing and reconstructing the data acquired from the image, however, the traditional SPI reconstruction algorithm reconstructs the image with more detail texture missing and serious artifacts at low sampling rates. To address this problem, this paper proposes an SPI reconstruction algorithm based on residual in-channel attention block (RICAB-GAN). In the proposed reconstruction algorithm, we improve the residual block in the generator network by adding channel attention (CA), which enables the network to notice more texture details in the image. In the discriminator network we remove all the BN layers to reduce the artifacts in the image and improve the generalization ability of the model. Through simulation experiments, our algorithm improves psnr by 1-5dB, ssim by 0.1-0.3, and retains image details and textures better than traditional SPI algorithms at low sampling rates.

articleTitle: Comparative Study on Intelligent Modulation Recognition Models Based on Raw Data
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: In recent years, intelligent modulation recognition methods for communication signals based on deep learning have attracted attention due to their advantages in feature extraction and recognition performance. However, there is limited research on the performance boundaries and optimization criteria of neural network models in existing domestic and international studies, and the datasets used in the research are relatively simple. This paper first proposes an intelligent modulation recognition model based on deep learning; Then a super dataset containing 22 traditional and emerging complex modulation modes is generated by simulation; Finally, based on this dataset, a comprehensive comparative analysis is conducted from multiple perspectives to investigate the effects of data slicing, selection and design of network models and parameters on the modulation recognition performance of the model. General patterns were obtained, providing valuable references for subsequent research and model application.

articleTitle: Research on Demand Forecasting Method of Shared Bicycle Based on Ensemble Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: With the continuous acceleration of urbanization, bike-sharing has become a convenient, environmentally friendly, and healthy way of travel. To alleviate the imbalance of shared bicycle demand, this paper designs a stacked random forest support vector machine regression ensemble model (RF-SVR) and a weighted average random forest support vector machine regression ensemble model. To verify the effectiveness of the design method, experiments were conducted on hourly bicycle rental datasets from Washington, D.C., USA from 2011 to 2012. Compared with the random forest regression model (RF) and support vector machine regression model (SVR), the experimental results show that the performance of the ensemble learning method is better than or equivalent to the single regression model under the evaluation index of RMSLE.

articleTitle: Research on Multimodal Emotion Recognition Based on Double Deep Networks and FR-ABCR
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: This paper proposes a new multi-mode emotion recognition method to improve the emotion recognition rate. The outstanding characteristic of this study are：1) Making full use of deep learning model can extract deep abstract features of emotional signals. a multimodal emotion feature extraction method based on double deep networks is proposed, which can not only effectively represent the characteristics of emotion, but also reduce the amount of calculation; 2) Use the deep residual network as the basic convolutional neural network model, the degradation and gradient disappearance of deep convolutional neural networks due to increasing depth are solved; 3) According to the ensemble learning ideas for common decision of multiple classifiers, a multimodel emotion information fusion and recognition algorithm based on AdaBoost and Class Reliability (FR-ABCR) is proposed. Both the decision level and the feature level are integrated, so that the whole emotion category recognition process is closer to the process of human brain judgment of emotion. Simulation experiments with a large number of data also prove the reliability and effectiveness of the proposed emotion recognition method.

articleTitle: Masked Face Recognition Method with Dual-branch Attention
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Air pollution and the presence of toxic gases in daily life pose a significant health concern, leading people to wear masks for protection. However, wearing masks obscures important facial features, consequently diminishing the performance of existing recognition methods. To tackle this issue, this study introduces a dual-branch attention-based method for recognizing masked faces. The method incorporates ECSA(Efficient Channel Spatial Attention) and N-UPA(New Upper Part Attention) modules and employs a dual-branch training structure. Each convolution block incorporates ECSA modules to improve the network’s ability to extract overall facial features. Additionally, a branch network comprising the N-UPA module is introduced to focus on extracting features from the eye area, thereby enhancing the accuracy of mask face recognition. The effectiveness of the proposed method has been validated using a real dataset. Experimental results showcase its exceptional generalization capability. Moreover, in comparison to advanced methods, the proposed approach markedly improves the performance of recognizing faces under mask occlusion.

articleTitle: Application of Improved Canny Algorithm in Image Edge Detection of Transmission Lines
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Aiming at the incoherence and inaccuracy of traditional canny algorithm for transmission line image edge detection, an improved Canny algorithm is proposed for transmission line image edge detection. Firstly, the adaptive median filter is used instead of the traditional Gaussian filter to denoise the image, and the edge details can be preserved better. To solve the problem of single template of traditional Canny operator, gradient templates in horizontal, vertical, 45° and 135° are used to calculate the image gradient, which reduces the error detection rate and edge loss. Then the non-maximum value is suppressed by linear interpolation to make the edge information more accurate. Finally, in view of the limitation of traditional Canny operators artificially setting high and low thresholds, the maximum interclass difference method is used to calculate the high and low thresholds according to the image gray scale, so as to enhance the adaptability. The experimental results show that in comparison with traditional Canny algorithm, the improved Canny operator has better continuity and integrity in image edge extraction of transmission lines, and has obvious advantages.

articleTitle: Video Behavior Recognition Model Based on 3D Reprameterized Convolution
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: In addressing the challenge posed by the extensive parameters of 3D convolutional modules, this paper extends the 2D reparameterization method to propose a 3D reparameterized convolutional module. During training, this module capitalizes on a multi-path structure for effective feature learning, while simplifying into a single-path structure during deployment to curtail computational costs. Moreover, to enhance the model's focus on the temporal dimension, a channel-time attention module is introduced, further augmenting the model's accuracy. Leveraging these modules, a reparameterized 3D convolutional neural network is developed for video behavior recognition. Experimental results underscore the efficacy of the proposed modules, showcasing improved model accuracy and reduced inference time.

articleTitle: Research and implementation of method for identifying body conflict behaviors of drivers and passgeners
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: In order to enhance the safety of passengers and lessen the impact of physical dispute on people safety, this article proposes an efficient identification method that can be deployed on RK1808 using NPU to accelerate offline detection of physical conflicts between drivers and passengers. The method first uses object detection algorithms to detect the positions of passengers in the car, and then uses the HRnet algorithm to detect 13 skeletal key points on the upper body of the human body. By calculating the distance between the corresponding keypoints of two individuals, it is possible to determine whether there is physical conflict between the driver and the passenger.To verify the feasibility of the method, we built a dataset of physical conflicts in the car, including data from both day and night, and recorded various physical conflicts between front and rear passengers and drivers. Through experimental results, it can be found that the Yolov5+HRnet manner can precisely identify physical conflicts during the day and at night. The recognition accuracy of behaviors such as front passengers pulling the driver’s arm, attacking the driver’s head, the driver fighting back, rear passengers attacking the driver, and normal driving can all approach 90%. Therefore, the manner put forward in this article has high functional value and application prospects.

Author Keywords: Key point detection of human skeleton

articleTitle: Dense Video Captioning Based on Memory Enhanced Attention and Guided Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: In the task of captioning multiple events in video content, traditional models using self-attention mechanisms often suffer from the problem of missing fine-grained visual semantic details due to the complexity and diversity of the content. The long-tail distribution of words in the video corpus further exacerbates the insufficient training of words related to visual content, which in turn affects the accuracy of video captions. Therefore, this paper proposes a Memory-Enhanced Attention Network that utilizes a memory module to capture the importance of frame-level features. It combines the historical visual semantic information and performs weighted fusion to select and control the flow, enabling the model to capture complex visual semantic information and better capture long-range inter-frame correlations, thus addressing the problem of missing visual semantic details.Additionally, the paper introduces a guided learning cross-entropy loss function that incorporates rich linguistic knowledge into the model using a pre-trained language model (ELM). By minimizing the KL divergence between the predicted word distribution and the ELM probability distribution at the sentence level, the model's caption accuracy is improved, alleviating the long-tail word distribution problem in the video corpus. Experimental results on the ActivityNet Captions and YouCook2 datasets demonstrate that the proposed approach outperforms other state-of-the-art models.

articleTitle: Lightwight Image Super-Resolution: The Shift Ladder Transformer Approach
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: In lightweight Super Resolution (SR) tasks, balancing performance and efficiency is a challenge for CNN-based models. The Transformer architecture has been introduced into super-resolution tasks due to its global self-attention mechanism. However, existing lightweight image super-resolution networks based on Transformers typically employ localized attention to sparsify their attention, thereby limiting their receptive field and uniformity of pixel weight distribution. To address these challenges, this paper introduces the Shift Ladder Transformer for Super Resolution (slTSR), a lightweight model that melds lightweight convolutional layers with a distinct residual Shift Ladder Transformer block. With the integration of the Shift Ladder Transformer Layer (SLTL) strategy, slTSR effectively amalgamates information from diverse spatial windows, enhancing information exchange. Experiments on diverse datasets consistently highlight the exceptional performance and efficiency of slTSR.

articleTitle: Spiking-Timing-Dependent Plasticity Convolutional Spiking Neural Network for Efficient Radar-Based Gesture Recognition
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: An innovative architecture, termed Spike-Timing-Dependent Plasticity Convolutional Spiking Neural Network (STDP-CSNN), is proposed for efficient radar-based gesture recognition in this paper. Radar range-Doppler image data are encoded into spike sequences with CSNN, and the leaky integrate-and-fire (LIF) model is employed as a neuron in the network nodes. This design enables efficient accumulation and transmission of spike signals, resulting in a significant reduction in network power consumption. Furthermore, the unsupervised learning algorithm of STDP is employed to facilitate feature extraction in the established CSNN, ensuring low computational complexity. The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed STDP-CSNN architecture achieves an impressive recognition accuracy of 92.72%, while concurrently addressing the crucial requirements of low power consumption and computational simplicity.

articleTitle: An Efficient Convolutional Multi-Scale Vision Transformer for Image Classification
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: This paper introduces an innovative and efficient multi-scale Vision Transformer (ViT) for the task of image classification. The proposed model leverages the inherent power of transformer architecture and combines it with the concept of multi-scale processing generally used in convolutional neural networks (CNNs). The work aims to address the limitations of conventional ViTs which typically operate at a single scale, hence overlooking the hierarchical structure in visual data. The multi-scale ViT enhances classification performance by processing image features at different scales, effectively capturing both low-level and high-level semantic information. Extensive experimental results demonstrate the superior performance of the proposed model over standard ViTs and other state-of-the-art image classification methods, signifying the effectiveness of the multi-scale approach. This research opens new avenues for incorporating scale-variance in transformer-based models for improved performance in vision tasks.

articleTitle: Industrial Inspection Auxiliary System Based On AR Technology
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: This paper proposes an artificial inspection auxiliary system based on AR technology to achieve high quality and efficiency in industrial inspection. The real scene is superimposed with virtual information via the AR terminal, and the inspection work is analyzed, guided, and decided, effectively assisting the artificial inspection work. To identify and match the equipment, SURF’s scale invariance and efficient identification performance are used. The high-precision indoor positioning of the tunnel 5G, the POI information of the object, the direction angle sensor in the AR intelligent terminal, and other data information are used to establish identification and matching based on the unique attributes of the target object, which greatly improves the accuracy of identification and matching. The system’s real-time data and decision-making function can reduce the average inspection time to 59% of that of traditional artificial inspection. The AR auxiliary inspection system-planned inspection route effectively avoids missed inspections, and overall inspection accuracy is close to 93%, effectively improving inspection quality and efficiency.

articleTitle: Comparison of Large Language And Vision Models on Representative Downstream Tasks
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: The success of large model pre-training in the fields of natural language processing and computer vision has been remarkable. By pre-training on large-scale data, these models can learn richer semantic and visual representations to achieve better performance on various tasks. performance. In order to enable more researchers and practitioners to fully understand the advantages and applicable fields of different models, this paper summarizes the current large model pre-training methods, including Vision Transformer (ViT), Pre-trained Transformer (GPT), Text-to-Text Transfer Transformer (T5), Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers (BERT) and Contrastive Language-Image Pretraining (CLIP) are all included, and discusses their principles and advantages are presented. At the same time, compare their results are compared on different datasets, and compare the results of combining them with different other techniques. The final research results show that ViT has advantages over other models in image classification, GPT performs best in generative tasks compared to other models, and T5 has achieved significant results in various text tasks compared to other models, while BERT performs best in various discriminative tasks compared to other models. CLIP is suitable for image and text-related tasks, including image classification, text retrieval, visual question answering, etc. Finally, applications of various models are summarized, providing direction for researchers and practitioners.

articleTitle: Application of Band Combination in Landslide Identification of Remote Sensing Images Driven by Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: With the frequent occurrence of geological disasters, landslide identification has become an important research problem. In recent years, with the application and research of deep learning in the fields of computer vision and remote sensing image analysis, deep learning has become a popular method for landslide identification research because of its excellent feature extraction and pattern recognition capabilities. In this paper, we add new bands reflecting vegetation and water of landslide factors to the original bands of remote sensing image samples by linear combination of bands, and conduct two sets of comparison experiments on Unet and Swin-Unet to verify that adding band features can help improve landslide identification accuracy. The experimental results show that the experimental group with additional band features has a numerical improvement in landslide identification accuracy, with F1-score as the evaluation index, the Unet experimental group has a 2.29% improvement and the Swin-Unet experimental group has a 1.78% improvement. The results of this paper have implications for the subsequent application of bands combination of landslide factor features in remote sensing landslide identification driven by deep learning methods.

articleTitle: Evaluation of spatial layout of urban road landscape based on deep learning
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: In recent years, artificial intelligence has made great breakthroughs in deep learning, and this paper aims to explore the innovative development of deep learning to conduct in-depth analysis and research on the layout of urban road landscapes. Road landscape is a part of the urban structure and one of the prominent characteristics of the city, a good and beautiful road landscape is conducive to the positive development of the city. This paper aims to combine deep learning to better meet people’s aesthetic needs and spatial experience of urban road landscape.

articleTitle: Research on Key Technologies for Deep Optimization of Unity Based Scenarios
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: With the gradual expansion of the scale of virtual reality scenes, a large amount of real-time rendering is required during the operation of the scene, which will reduce the real-time interactivity of the scene, thereby affecting the user experience of browsing virtual scenes<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">[1]</sup>.Therefore, in response to these issues, we optimize and explore the virtual scene of Unity3D, and use UPR testing tools to optimize in the Unity scene. Through testing results and application solutions, and analysis, we elucidate their impact on the performance of the central processing unit and graphics processor. This has important significance for improving the real-time performance of virtual reality interaction, and helps to improve the speed of scene operation and thus improve the user experience.

articleTitle: An Improved Depth Image Clustering Algorithm Based on Spatial Information
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Depth image spatial clustering is an important task in the fields of computer vision and machine learning, aiming to group pixels or point cloud data of depth images into clusters with similar features. This is crucial for tasks such as object recognition, scene segmentation, 3D reconstruction, and other applications. The K-means algorithm is a commonly used clustering method that divides data points into K clusters, ensuring that each data point belongs to the cluster whose center is closest to it. However, traditional K-means algorithms face several challenges in depth image spatial clustering, such as sensitivity to the choice of K and the influence of cluster center initialization on the results. In this study, we propose an improved depth image clustering method based on spatial information. The method includes depth image edge extraction, intra-edge region growing, unclassified point re-clustering, and connected region merging. Through experiments conducted on datasets from TUM, Bonn, and our collected data, our algorithm demonstrates superior performance in depth image clustering tasks, higher clustering accuracy, fewer unclassified points, and faster convergence speed.

articleTitle: One Shot Face Image Style Transfer Method Based on GAN
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Style transformation on face images has traditionally been a popular research area in the field of computer vision, and its applications are quite extensive. Currently, the more mainstream schemes include Generative Adversarial Network (GAN)-based image generation as well as style transformation and Stable diffusion method. In 2019, the NVIDIA team proposed StyleGAN, which is a relatively mature scheme for generating real faces as well as face feature blending. The whole StyleGAN model is trained based on the Flickr-Faces-HQ Dataset (FFHQ) dataset, the This is a large dataset, so the model takes a long time to train. My aim is to form a One-shot stylized face image generator, which means that only one reference face and one stylized face need to be input, and a brand-new face with a mixture of features can be generated in a short training time. This is inspired by the existing research result JoJoGAN, which learns a style mapper from a single example of the style. JoJoGAN uses a GAN inversion procedure and StyleGAN's style-mixing property to produce a substantial paired dataset from a single example of the style. This paper will make improvements to JoJoGAN, including improving the encoder that utilizes the GAN Inversion method to generate latent codes for image features, and the random mixing of latent codes to produce a more refined paired dataset.

articleTitle: De-Beauty GAN: Restore the original beauty of the face
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Changes in face makeup and facial morphology pose new challenges for face recognition, and recent developments in image translation have laid the technological foundation for the de-beautification task. To this end, the first publicly available dataset containing 36,000 multi-ethnic and gender images rich in facial beauty, especially facial morphology changes, is established. Based on this dataset, we propose De-Beauty GAN, a highly scalable and robust facial de-beauty model that can synthesize more realistic de-beautified faces. Unlike existing de-beauty models, the model proposed in this paper considers the recovery of facial deformation. According to the characteristics of the image processing task, a new quantitative metric, DBE, for de-beauty evaluation is proposed, and the usability of this metric is evaluated through quantization. The experimental results demonstrate that the model proposed in this paper can effectively handle the de-beautification task with 1.3 and 1.6 times better results than the existing popular methods, respectively.

articleTitle: A Uyghur text detection method in natural scenes based on improved CenterNet
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Aiming at the problems of difficult Uyghur feature extraction, easy missed detection of targets and low detection efficiency, a Uyghur text detection method based on CenterNet is proposed. Firstly, the lightweight EfficientNetV2-S is used as the backbone network to reduce the network parameters and improve the ability of the network to extract features. Then, the SE module in the backbone network EfficientNetV2-S is replaced by the ECA module to improve the network operation speed of the network. In addition, according to the characteristics of the diversity of Uyghur target size, the deconvolution module in CenterNet is removed, and the pyramid network of features is introduced to enhance the adaptability of the model to Uyghur with different target sizes and improve the generalization ability of the model. The experimental results on the Uyghur dataset show that the average precision of the improved CenterNet for Uyghur detection in natural scenes reaches 94.2 %, which is 5.9 % higher than that of the original CenterNet, and the detection effect on Uyghur is better.

articleTitle: Exploration of Lightweight Neural Network Architectures for Sentiment Analysis
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: The increasing computational burden associated with traditional Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) and Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs) is driving the need for lightweight, efficient models, particularly for edge computing and low-power devices. This study explores the performance and computational costs of various lightweight neural network architectures, including Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), SimpleRNN, and multiple versions of 1D CNNs, as well as a 1D ResNet and a DenseNet model. The experimental setup evaluates each model across the same problem domain, with the intention of determining the most efficient and effective architecture. Methods involved layering combinations of convolutional, pooling, normalization, dropout, and densely connected layers. Some models were augmented with advanced techniques like residual connections and learning rate decay for better performance and generalization. Results indicate that simplified 1D CNNs perform remarkably well in terms of both accuracy and training efficiency. More specifically, 1D CNN models achieved comparable or better performance metrics than their LSTM and SimpleRNN counterparts, with significantly lower computational costs. This was particularly true for CNN models with simpler architectures, emphasizing the possibility of achieving high performance with reduced complexity. In conclusion, findings provide strong evidence that simpler 1D CNN models can serve as effective and computationally inexpensive alternatives to more complex neural network architectures, potentially facilitating broader adoption in resource constrained environments.

articleTitle: Research on overload detection of trucks based on multi-sensor information fusion
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach for detecting truck overloads using a non-contact multi-sensor fusion method. The motivation behind this research stems from the limitations of existing highway truck overload detection systems, which suffer from low accuracy and challenging equipment maintenance. Initially, the collection of infrared temperature and sound data from the vehicle is facilitated through the utilization of infrared thermal camera and sound sensor devices that are positioned along the route. Second, the extracted infrared feature data are fused with the sound feature data for feature fusion, while principal component analysis (PCA) is utilized to reduce the data's dimensionality. Finally, the integration of the Flower Pollination method (FPA) and the Support Vector Machine (SVM) method is employed to develop a model for detecting truck overload. This model, known as EFPA-SVM, utilizes multi-feature fusion classification. The results of the tests indicate that the detection accuracy for identifying the true presence of 200 overloaded trucks is 82.3%. Additionally, it is feasible to achieve non-contact detection of lorry overload by combining temperature and auditory data. This research holds significance for the management of overloaded trucks.

articleTitle: A multi-view stable feature extraction network for SAR target recognition
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Since the viewing angle sensitivity of Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) image, targets’ shape changes dramatically in different viewing angle, the accuracy of SAR target recognition base on deep learning in single view is often affected by this difference between various viewing angle of SAR. So the multi-view approaches have been proposed to solve this limitation by learning the targets’ relationships between images from different viewings. In this paper, a multi-view stable feature extraction network (MV-SFN) is proposed which constructs stable feature that doesn’t change with viewing angle by using multi-view images. It uses Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) to gain image feature, then take Gate Recurrent Unit (GRU) to analyze varying regularity of series viewing features. At last a novel features fusion module was designed for fusing different viewing features according to their similarity, and finally going to classify. MSTAR database is used to validate MV-SFN method.

articleTitle: Hard Example Mining-based Training Strategy for Pointly-Supervised Instance Segmentation
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: The time-consuming task of generating mask-level annotations has impeded the extensive adoption of instance segmentation. To address this challenge, weakly-supervised instance segmentation has emerged, leveraging more available annotation types to achieve performance comparable to fully-supervised approaches. Recent advancements in pointly-supervised instance segmentation demonstrate promising outcomes by employing a mere 20 labeled points within bounding box per object. This approach substantially decreases the annotation burden while preserving competitive performance levels. However, its indiscriminate training strategy for all labeled points severely limits the segmentation performance of the model. In this paper, we propose a novel Hard Example Mining-based Training Strategy for pointly-supervised instance segmentation, effectively utilizing limited point-based supervision and focusing on challenging labeled points. Our method addresses the need for efficient supervision by leveraging sparse point annotations while maintaining competitive performance. On COCO, we show that models trained with our strategy yield significantly gain compared against normal training strategy.

articleTitle: Heterogeneous deep graph convolutional network with iterative deep graph learning for Covid-19 inline recommendation
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Covid-19 has been causing persistent negative impact on people’s daily life all over the world. A mass of scientific literature in medicine and biology has been published since then. It could be a hard process to gather the needed papers for researchers and scientists. Many approaches have been proposed to generate inline recommendation list for paper searching. However, the previous methods have some defects. For example, the content-based method only focuses on the full text but neglects the citation relation. Some other deep learning methods did not take the refresh of graph structure into consideration. Hence, this paper presents a new deep learning method for the COVID-19 citation recommendation task. Two main parts are included in this method. The first part, iterative deep graph learning (IDGL), is to optimize the graph structure by iterating the similarity learning process. The second part, heterogeneous deep graph convolution network (HDGCN), is to learn effective dense node vectors. The node embedding vectors are first initialized by BioBERT and put into the heterogeneous graph convolution layer. The heterogenous graph convolution layer learns the graph with nodes of different features. Then the data flows into the deep attention layer, which reweights node importance using the trainable vectors simultaneously. Finally, the data goes through the decoder layer to recover the graph structure and generates the recommendation list based on the similarity score. It is proved that the method presented in this paper performs better than the previous methods on the CORD-19 dataset and Litcovid dataset.

articleTitle: KL-Weighted Graph Sparse Self-Representation for Unsupervised Hyperspectral Band Selection
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Unsupervised band selection (BS) methods have attracted much attention in hyperspectral imagery (HSI), which can select informative bands to solve the problems of information redundancy and high computational complexity. In this paper, we propose a KL-weighted graph sparse self-representation (SSR) method for unsupervised BS, in which the dissimilarity of bands measured via KL divergence is integrated into the superpixel-based graph SSR model by weighting the sparse representation coefficient matrix. An alternating optimization algorithm is designed to obtain the optimal coefficient matrix and the representative bands are finally selected by the norm ranking of rows of the coefficient matrix. Experimental results on HIS datasets show the effectiveness of the proposed BS algorithm and it outperforms other related BS methods in selecting proper representative bands for classification.

articleTitle: Deep Convolutional Neural Networks for Rail Surface Defect Perception
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Rail surface defect inspection is a vital element for ensuring railway safety. We critically analyze the application of deep convolutional neural networks (CNN) in Rail Surface Defect Perception (RSDP). We scrutinize 43 studies, revealing how CNN, YOLO, R-CNN, and Semantic Segmentation techniques, have revolutionized RSDP by surpassing traditional inspection methods in speed, accuracy, and efficiency. Our examination underscores the necessity for comprehensive and standardized datasets to support the varied and complex nature of rail surface defects. Additionally, we highlight the persistent challenges such as limited defect samples and the imperative for real-time detection capabilities. The paper details the performance and adaptation of various CNN models for RSDP, charting a course for future inquiry. We advocate for enhanced datasets, unified defect classification, and refined deep learning models, aiming to bolster the progress in CNN-driven RSDP technology for enhanced railway safety.

articleTitle: End-to-End Person Search Based on Content Awareness
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Within the domain of computer vision, person search stands out as a crucial and intricate undertaking. With the growth of urban population and the popularity of surveillance cameras, person search demonstrates its versatility in a multitude of applications, particularly within the realm of video surveillance, public safety and intelligent transportation. The person search task is comprised of two subtasks, namely person detection and person re-identification (ReID),the task of person detection concentrates on identifying similarities among diverse identities. In contrast, person ReID task centres on discovering dissimilarities among distinct identities. In order to reduce the influence of variations in tasks during the model training phase, we segment the ResNet50 network according to the subtasks and propose an end-to-end content-aware person search framework. Where the detection branch is built on top of shallow features and the person ReID branch is built on top of deep features. Meanwhile, we introduce gated deformable convolution module(GDCM)to sense the location of the person and further distinguish the background from the person. Finally, the effectiveness of the method is demonstrated on two authoritative datasets(CUHK-SYSU、PRW) .

articleTitle: A classification study of pulmonary nodule CT images based on supervised contrast learning
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: With the increasing amount of pulmonary odule CT images and the difficulty of labeling categories, traditional deep learning methods that rely on labeled samples may not be able to learn effectively. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a 3D convolutional network for pulmonary nodule feature extraction using contrastive learning. The proposed method consists of two phases: discriminative feature learning and classification. In the discriminative feature learning phase, a supervised contrast learning loss is used to reduce the distance between nodules in the same class while increasing the distance between nodules in different classes, thus improving intra-class diversity and inter-class similarity. In the subsequent classification phase, pre-training weights are fine-tuned to better fit the LUNA16 dataset. The proposed network achieves an accuracy of 86.96, an F1-score of 81.28, and a mean G-mean of 83.86 on the LUNA16 dataset. Compared with existing supervised learning methods, introducing contrastive learning allows for the full use of labeled data and improves the classification accuracy of lung nodules with the same amount of training data.

articleTitle: An intelligent measurement method for air preheater clearance
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: To satisfy the needs of thermal power plants for monitoring the boiler air preheater distance between the bottom edge of the fan plate and the rotor ring shroud in high-temperature environments, an intelligent measurement method for air preheater clearance is proposed. First, a set of hardware-assisted schemes combined with computer vision technology is designed, which enables efficient and accurate identification and localization of the measurement target. Then, the pixel distance is remapped using neural network technology to reduce measurement errors caused by image distortion and the placement of camera equipment. The experimental results show that this method is feasible, efficient, and robust, and the measurement accuracy can reach ±1.25mm with a maximum relative error of 1.14 percent.

articleTitle: A Preprocessing Method for Fragment Perforation Image Detection
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: The perforation data left by the fragments generated by the explosion of ammunition warheads on the surrounding metal plates can reflect the dispersion characteristics of the fragments, which is a commonly used ammunition power testing method. Using image detection based methods to analyze metal plate perforation images can quickly and accurately detect the number and size of fragment perforation. Therefore, image quality is crucial for the accuracy of the analysis results. This study proposes an image preprocessing method for detecting metal plate perforation images, and compares and analyzes the effects of different filtering methods, morphological processing methods, and perforation edge detection methods on the image preprocessing results, The results show that using median filtering, open operation morphological processing methods, and edge detection methods based on Gaussian fitting models can obtain preprocessed images that better reflect the true bullet hole information.

articleTitle: A multimodal registration network based on triplet loss and transformer
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: At this stage, although the problem of unimodal image alignment has been largely solved, the problem of multimodal image alignment still does not have a good solution. Although multimodality has richer and more comprehensive information than unimodality, the fact that multimodal images come from different imaging devices while traditional unimodal multi-view image alignment algorithms only consider extracting features from the images generated by the same type of imaging devices during feature extraction leads to such algorithms not being able to be applied directly to multimodal image alignment. Taking infrared-visible image registration as an example, we propose a feature extraction method for multi-source images. Experiments have shown that applying the proposed method to cross-modal image alignment tasks can significantly increase the number of successful alignments, demonstrating the effectiveness of this method.

articleTitle: Frequency Filtering Network for Undersampled MRI Reconstruction
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is an imaging technology widely used in medical clinical diagnosis. Nevertheless, it always takes a long imaging time to obtain the high spatial resolution MR image. Image reconstruction has been playing a crucial role for accelerated MRI. Recently, deep neural networks show potential to significantly speed up MRI. However, these deep learning methods usually learn the feature information in the spatial domain. Although some works have attempted to utilize the frequency information from the k-space to reconstruct MR images, they still suffer from the inability to consider the global information. To address these limitations, in this work, we propose a new residual filter channel attention network (RFCAN) for undersampled MRI reconstruction. Specifically, the proposed model consists of a novel filter channel attention (FCA) in the frequency domain and the multiscale cascade convolution in the spatial domain to learn both the dual-domain features. This model employs the filtering instead of the traditional self-attention mechanism in Transformer to learn k-space information. It can avoid the limitations of the Transformer window to better learn the global information. We also introduce a frequency channel attention to fine-tune the filtering results to better balance the global and local information. Experiment results show that our model consistently outperforms other state-of-the-art methods and can achieve high-quality MRI reconstruction.

articleTitle: Edge End Safety Helmet Wearing Detection Based on Detection Head Optimization
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Safety helmet wearing detection is an crucial means in safeguarding the lives of construction workers, but it often requires edge computing due to unstable networks and privacy concerns. In resource-constrained scenarios, the detection head of a model often accounts for an excessive amount of computation. Therefore, this study adopts RepConv, GhostConv, PConv, and GroupConv to reconstruct the shared parameters of the small model’s detection head and explores the performance of different models and the detection speed on Jetson Xavier NX. Among them, the detection head improved by RepConv increases the mean average precision (mAP) and F1 score of safety helmet wear detection by 0.6% and 0.72%, respectively, without increasing computation; the detection head improved by PConv increases the frames per second (FPS) of the model by 20.10% and reduces computation by 1/3. Overall, there is still great potential for improving the detection head.

articleTitle: Multi-objective Optimization of Residential Energy Consumption Based on Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: This paper delves into the application of machine learning (ML) for predicting and optimizing energy consumption in residential buildings. By analyzing data from a typical twelve-story residential building in Ningbo, four distinct machine learning models—Ordinary Least Squares, Decision Tree Regression, Random Forest Regression, and Gaussian Process Regression—were employed for energy consumption forecasting. It was discovered that the Decision Tree and Gaussian Process Regression models excelled in energy consumption prediction, closely aligning with the actual data, while the Ordinary Least Squares model exhibited larger prediction errors. The study provides valuable insights for energy-saving and emission reduction in residential buildings, showcasing the potential of ML in building energy management. It underscores the importance of accurate data collection and foresees the amalgamation of smart home technology and ML insights to foster energy-efficient, real-time responsive living spaces.

articleTitle: Research on Crack Size Identification Method Based on Digital Image Processing Technology
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Cracks is one of the common hazards in offshore structures, and continuous crack propagation can cause serious consequences such as steel structure fracture. The steel structure adopts a regular inspection method to detect structural cracks. Once cracks are found, emergency repair and maintenance work is carried out to ensure the safety of the structure. One of the keys of crack visual inspection is to accurately extract crack size from image. Based on digital image processing technology, the camera calibration, image processing and crack feature extraction were achieved by OpenCV and Skimage open source algorithm package, and then the crack pixel size was extracted. The crack pixel size is converted to the actual size by pixel calibration. The crack length inspection error is 4.8%, and the maximum width inspection error is 13.7%. The results show that the crack identification method has high crack inspection accuracy,which is worth spreading and applying.

articleTitle: Traffic sign recognition in complex environments based on YOLOv5
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: To address the issue of difficulty in recognizing traffic signs in complex environments and the lack of accuracy, a traffic sign recognition model based on YOLOv5 in complex environments is proposed. Firstly, optimize the target detection layer and further reduce the size of the detection head to enhance the model's ability to extract features from small targets. Then, a cross-connection network is introduced into the network layer to effectively reduce the loss of feature information during network transmission. Finally, adaptive spatial feature fusion technology is used to strengthen the fusion of multi-scale feature information. Experimental results show that the traffic sign recognition in complex environments has reached 83.6%, 76.0%, and 82.2% in Precision, Recall and mAP@0.5 respectively. Compared with YOLOv5s, these three indicators have increased by 6.4%, 3.1%, and 4.7% respectively. Moreover, the model's parameter amount has decreased by 5.6%, making the model more lightweight.

articleTitle: Improvement of Voxel Down-Sampling Method in Point Cloud Registration
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: In order to mitigate the influence of outliers in point clouds on voxel down-sampling results and the accuracy of point cloud registration in practical applications, the voxel down-sampling method in the Point Cloud Library (PCL) has been improved. First, the nearest-neighbor distance method is applied to search for the actual point that is closest to the calculated centroid point of a voxel volume. This point is then used as the reserved point to replace the voxel, which helps to preserve the local detailed features of the edge contour of the point cloud. Secondly, considering that the voxels located at the edges of a point cloud often contain a large number of outliers and these outliers are characterized by a sparse distribution, a constraint of a minimum number of points is imposed to effectively eliminate outliers in the edge area and greatly reduce their impact on the accuracy of point cloud registration. Down-sampling and registration experiments were conducted using Bunny point clouds provided by Stanford University. The experimental results demonstrate that the improved voxel down-sampling method effectively improves the accuracy and speed of point cloud registration.

articleTitle: A Novel Point Cloud Coarse Registration Method Combining 2D image information
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Point cloud registration is one of the key technologies for point cloud data processing. Feature descriptor-based point cloud registration methods have been widely adopted for point cloud registration. However, these methods demand a high overlap between the point clouds to be registered, struggle to acquire matched points, and involve extensive computations. To address the above issues, a novel point cloud coarse registration method combining 2D image information is proposed in this paper. This method introduces a checkerboard and utilizes a 3D structured light depth camera to simultaneously acquire point cloud data and 2D images of the target scene. Based on camera imaging principles, corner points are extracted from 2D images and camera poses are estimated to obtain matched points for point clouds, thereby fitting a rigid transformation to achieve point cloud coarse registration. The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method is minimally influenced by point cloud overlap rate, and can achieve accurate and efficient point cloud registration.

articleTitle: Research on indoor robot navigation algorithm based on deep reinforcement learning
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Highly intelligent robot is the trend in the new round of development, and it is also the ultimate goal of robot navigation technology research.The ability to learn is an important embodiment of robot intelligence.Autonomous navigation is the basic function of indoor mobile robots<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">[1]</sup>and it is the premise and key technology to realize the autonomy and intelligence of robots.With the continuous development of robot-related technologies and the continuous expansion of application scope, the tasks faced by robots are more challenging, and the work scenes are increasingly complex and diversified, which puts forward new requirements and challenges for navigation technology. Indoor robot navigation systems need not only to maintain accuracy and stability in fixed scenes, but also to be able to handle dynamic changes in the environment, and to take into account safety and the impact on human comfort in an environment that coexists with humans.This paper takes the indoor mobile robot platform as the research object<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">[2]</sup>, introduces the machine learning algorithm based on neural network into the navigation task<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">[3]</sup>, utilizes the existing research achievements in the field of deep learning to build a robot navigation system based on different learning modes, and endows the robot with intelligent perception ability and navigation strategy learning ability<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">[4]</sup>.

articleTitle: TFA Block: Temporal Feature Alignment Block for Video Frame interpolation
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Video frame interpolation is an important low-level task in the field of image processing, which is widely applied to video image restoration enhancement, media players and display devices. In this work, we design an optical flow module, termed TFA block, for temporal feature alignment based on spatial-temporal modeling for fast and accurate video frame interpolation. It first matches adjacent input frames into spatial location roughly, then uses spatial-temporal modeling to align spatial features with time domain, and finally merges in time domain dimension to obtain optical flow between input continuous frames and objective frame. TFA block does not need complex network structure or relying on the pre-trained optical flow network, but obtain the task-oriented bidirectional intermediate optical flow from output frame to given inputs for backward warping. Compared to the state-of-the-art (SOTA) algorithms, our network achieves demonstrates both excellent performance improvement and fast inference speed

articleTitle: VDD4TS: A Vehicle Detection Dataset for Traffic Survey of Road
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: While object detection has achieved remarkable success in tasks such as autonomous driving and intelligent transportation, there is still a gap in meeting the fine-grained detection requirements for specialized road traffic survey tasks. To address this, we built a dedicated vehicle detection dataset tailored for traffic surveys of roads, named the VDD4TS. Within monitoring scenarios, VDD4TS aims to perform detection research on ten vehicle categories, including sedans, small trucks, buses, medium-sized trucks, large trucks, extra-large vehicles, container trucks, tractors, motorcycles, and electric cars. It comprises 12,535 high-quality images, encompassing 59,242 bounding boxes. It accounts for diverse lighting and weather conditions. Furthermore, the dataset possesses three noteworthy attributes: more detailed vehicle classification, a specific focus on suburban and rural scenes that road network detection systems relatively less represent, and distinct and informative annotation details. Extensive baseline experiments were conducted in object detection tasks to validate the dataset's effectiveness. The experimental results indicate that the VDD4TS dataset poses challenges for current mainstream object detection algorithms and is suitable for evaluating more complex advanced algorithmic models.

articleTitle: Leveraging Knowledge Distillation for Efficient Deep Reinforcement Learning in Resource-Constrained Environments
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: This paper aims to explore the potential of combining Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) with Knowledge Distillation (KD) by distilling various DRL algorithms and studying their distillation effects. By doing so, the computational burden of deep models could be reduced while maintaining the performance. The primary objective is to provide a benchmark for evaluating the performance of different DRL algorithms that have been refined using KD techniques. By distilling these algorithms, the goal is to develop efficient and fast DRL models.
